docs/site/research.html:17:</header> <main> <section class="learn-hero"> <div class="kicker">Interactive field guide · programming knowledge assumed · measurement science taught here</div> <p class="readme-eyebrow">From watts to warranted claims.</p> <h1>How do you measure<br>a machine thinking?</h1> <p class="lede">You already know how programs execute. This guide adds the uncomfortable part: deciding which physical signal belongs to the program, how much noise the instrument adds, and what the evidence actually permits you to say.</p> <nav class="chapter-nav" aria-label="Guide chapters"> <a href="#hard">The hard part</a><a href="#units">Watts &amp; joules</a> <a href="#sampling">Sampling</a><a href="#bundles">Bundles</a> <a href="#floor">Detection floors</a><a href="#found">Findings</a> <a href="#next">Next</a> </nav> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span> <span class="source-chip" title="docs/site_src/research.html · commit 05002b1"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>site_src/<wbr>research.html</span><span class="source-commit">commit 05002b1</span></span></div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="hard"> <div class="chapter-number">01</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Why this is hard</div> <h2>The model does not come with an energy return value.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A profiler can tell you which function consumed CPU time. Energy is a physical quantity observed through a separate instrument. You have to align two clocks, define a boundary, and decide what else was happening while the model ran.</p> <div class="concept-grid"> <article><span>Boundary</span><h3>Which power?</h3><p>SoC rails omit parts of the whole machine. Wall power includes more than the chip. Neither is automatically wrong; an unlabeled boundary is.</p></article> <article><span>Attribution</span><h3>Which interval?</h3><p>Load the model too late or stop sampling too early and the number answers a different question than the experiment config asked.</p></article> <article><span>Workload</span><h3>Which work?</h3><p>Prompt length, generated tokens, batching, caching, stop behavior, and content can all change the physical execution.</p></article> <article><span>Noise</span><h3>Which difference?</h3><p>Background activity, thermal state, sampling cadence, clock error, and run order can manufacture a small “effect.”</p></article> </div> <aside class="learn-aside"><strong>The measurement-science move:</strong> replace “I got a number” with “I defined a quantity, captured the evidence, bounded what could imitate it, and stated the claim ceiling.”</aside> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="units"> <div class="chapter-number">02</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Watts, joules, and idle</div> <h2>Power is a rate. Energy is the area.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A watt is one joule per second. If power changes over time, energy is the integral under the power trace. That identity is a unit definition—not a JouleWise measurement result.</p> <div class="equation-stack"> <div><span>instantaneous power</span><strong>P(t)</strong><small>watts = joules / second</small></div> <div><span>gross measured energy</span><strong>E = ∫ P(t) dt</strong><small>headline basis within the named boundary</small></div> <div><span>idle-subtracted energy</span><strong>E<sub>secondary</sub> = ∫ (P(t) − P<sub>idle</sub>) dt</strong><small>within-device secondary view only</small></div> </div> <p>Idle is not “free energy to erase.” It is an observed baseline under a stated condition. Subtracting it can help describe activity above baseline on one device, but it can distort comparisons: a high-idle device gets a larger subtraction. JouleWise therefore uses <strong>gross energy for every cross-device, cross-configuration, and split-vs-monolithic headline</strong>. Phase energy is gross-only.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="sampling"> <div class="chapter-number">03</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">How powermetrics sampling works</div> <h2>You never see the continuous curve.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede"><code>powermetrics</code> reports discrete samples from named Apple power rails. JouleWise aligns those samples with runtime events and integrates between explicit measured-window boundaries. Move the toy controls below: the underlying program is unchanged, but the estimated area changes when the window or sample pattern changes.</p> <div class="interactive-card" data-trace-lab> <div class="interactive-head"><div><span class="card-label">Toy trace · illustrative, not project evidence</span><h3>Drag the window and sample controls.</h3></div><span class="status-chip amber">local-only SVG + JS</span></div> <svg class="power-lab" viewBox="0 0 720 290" role="img" aria-labelledby="traceTitle traceDesc"> <title id="traceTitle">Interactive toy power trace</title> <desc id="traceDesc">A toy idle, prefill, decode, and cooldown power curve with adjustable integration window and sample points.</desc> <g class="lab-grid"><line x1="56" y1="35" x2="56" y2="246"/><line x1="56" y1="246" x2="694" y2="246"/><line x1="56" y1="176" x2="694" y2="176"/><line x1="56" y1="106" x2="694" y2="106"/><line x1="56" y1="36" x2="694" y2="36"/></g> <text class="lab-axis" x="12" y="42">power</text><text class="lab-axis" x="649" y="276">time →</text> <rect class="lab-window" data-window x="180" y="36" width="390" height="210"/> <path class="lab-area" data-trace-area d=""/><path class="lab-line" data-trace-line d=""/> <g data-samples></g> <line class="lab-handle" data-start-line x1="180" y1="30" x2="180" y2="252"/> <line class="lab-handle" data-end-line x1="570" y1="30" x2="570" y2="252"/> <text class="lab-label" x="82" y="226">idle</text><text class="lab-label" x="243" y="62">prefill</text><text class="lab-label" x="405" y="105">decode</text><text class="lab-label" x="600" y="226">cooldown</text> </svg> <div class="lab-controls"> <label>window start <input data-start type="range" min="5" max="70" value="22"><output data-start-out>22%</output></label> <label>window end <input data-end type="range" min="30" max="98" value="82"><output data-end-out>82%</output></label> <label>sample spacing <input data-spacing type="range" min="3" max="16" value="7"><output data-spacing-out>7%</output></label> <label>sample phase <input data-phase type="range" min="0" max="100" value="28"><output data-phase-out>28%</output></label> </div> <div class="lab-readouts" aria-live="polite"> <div><span>Toy gross energy · illustrative gross basis</span><strong data-gross-out>—</strong></div> <div><span>Toy idle-subtracted energy · illustrative within-device secondary</span><strong data-idle-out>—</strong></div> <div><span>Samples inside measured window</span><strong data-count-out>—</strong></div> </div> <p class="interactive-note">The orange curve is an invented signal. Cyan dots are discrete samples; the shaded band is the measured window. Real JouleWise bundles retain the trace and event markers so the integration can be replayed rather than trusted.</p> </div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="bundles"> <div class="chapter-number">04</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Strict validation and bundles</div> <h2>A bundle is a proof packet, not a CSV export.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">The run directory is deliberately boring: normalized configuration, metadata, timestamped events, raw power evidence, logs, model outputs, and summary metrics. The interesting part is what strict validation does with it.</p> <div class="bundle-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Run bundle artifacts flow through strict validation to a bounded claim"> <div class="bundle-box"><span>run bundle</span><code>config.json</code><code>metadata.json</code><code>events.jsonl</code><code>raw telemetry</code><code>outputs + logs</code><code>summary metrics</code></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">replay →</div> <div class="bundle-box validator-box"><span>strict validator</span><p>parse raw evidence</p><p>re-derive windows</p><p>recompute energy</p><p>check provenance</p><p>fail on mismatch</p></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">gate →</div> <div class="bundle-box claim-box"><span>claim ceiling</span><p>L0: auditability</p><p>L1: descriptive</p><p>L2+: only after floor, uncertainty, plan, and evidence gates</p></div> </div> <p><strong>Strict-valid does not mean scientifically conclusive.</strong> It means the recorded artifact is internally valid under the strict contract. A bundle can be strict-valid and still carry flags that prevent a comparison claim. That distinction matters in the newest floor data.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="floor"> <div class="chapter-number">05</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Detection floors</div> <h2>How small is too small to resolve?</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">Repeat the same condition and the measured energy moves anyway. The false-effect guard floor summarizes how large that repeat scatter—or an ABBA comparison artifact—can look. An effect below the applicable floor is <strong>not resolvable</strong>, not proven absent.</p> <div class="interactive-card floor-lab" data-floor-lab> <div class="interactive-head"><div><span class="card-label">Effect-versus-floor gate</span><h3>Try to clear a real verified floor.</h3></div><span class="status-chip">calibration logic</span></div> <label class="floor-select">Choose the applicable gate <select data-floor-select> <option value="0.527197" data-basis="gross request · absolute repeat">Gross mid-request absolute · 0.527197 J</option> <option value="0.909237" data-basis="gross request · comparative ABBA">Gross mid-request comparative · 0.909237 J</option> <option value="0.536632" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary">Idle-subtracted mid-request absolute · 0.536632 J</option> <option value="0.894215" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary comparative">Idle-subtracted mid-request comparative · 0.894215 J</option> <option value="1.738940" data-basis="gross prefill phase · governing gate">Gross prefill phase gate · 1.738940 J</option> <option value="1.026892" data-basis="gross decode phase · governing gate">Gross decode phase gate · 1.026892 J</option> <option value="4.922865" data-basis="gross suite-item · governing gate">Gross suite-item gate · 4.922865 J</option> <option value="24.618735" data-basis="gross suite-level · governing gate">Gross suite-level gate · 24.618735 J</option> </select> </label> <label class="effect-control">Hypothetical observed effect <input data-effect type="range" min="0" max="30" value="0.70" step="0.01"> <output data-effect-out>0.70 J</output> </label> <div class="floor-track" aria-hidden="true"><span data-floor-mark></span><i data-effect-mark></i></div> <div class="floor-verdict" data-floor-verdict aria-live="polite"></div> <p class="interactive-note">Clearing this numeric gate is necessary, not sufficient. It does not clear clock, sampling, uncertainty, contamination, multiplicity, correctness, or pre-registered analysis-plan gates.</p> </div> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md · commit 907ee58"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>phase_2/<wbr>detection_floor.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 907ee58</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="found"> <div class="chapter-number">06</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">What the project has found so far</div> <h2>Real floors, plus an important warning.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">The verified Window-A extraction reports the following false-effect guard floors. Comparative values use ABBA blocks; “gate” is the larger applicable absolute/comparative value. Every energy number states its D-067 basis.</p> <div class="table-scroll"> <table class="ledger measurement-table learn-floor-table"> <thead><tr><th>window</th><th>energy basis</th><th>verified floor</th><th>how to read it</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td>mid request · absolute</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>0.527197 J</td><td>repeat-scatter floor</td></tr> <tr><td>mid request · comparative</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>0.909237 J</td><td>ABBA comparison floor</td></tr> <tr><td>mid request · absolute</td><td>idle-subtracted · within-device secondary</td><td>0.536632 J</td><td>repeat-scatter floor</td></tr> <tr><td>mid request · comparative</td><td>idle-subtracted · within-device secondary</td><td>0.894215 J</td><td>ABBA comparison floor</td></tr> <tr><td>prefill phase</td><td>gross · phase basis</td><td>1.738940 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> <tr><td>decode phase</td><td>gross · phase basis</td><td>1.026892 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> <tr><td>suite item</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>4.922865 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> <tr><td>suite level</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>24.618735 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> </tbody> </table> </div> <aside class="evidence-warning"><strong>The warning is part of the result.</strong> The floor collection is strict-valid and collection-usable, yet every contributing bundle is claim-evidence flagged. Cross-device headlines stay gross-first and boundary-labeled.</p></article> </div> <div class="research-questions"> <h3>The research arc</h3> <p><strong>Q1:</strong> when can split inference reduce total gross energy? <strong>Q2:</strong> how does interconnect bandwidth move that crossover? <strong>Q3:</strong> what is the energy–latency trade? <strong>Q4:</strong> what fixed-plus-marginal model Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<p>Living register of risks that could sink, delay, or weaken the capstone. Review at the start of every phase and whenever a trigger fires; update statuses at the end of substantial runs alongside <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</p> <p>Conventions:</p> <ul> <li>Likelihood/Impact: low / medium / high, judged against the current phase.</li> <li>Trigger: the observable event that means the risk is materializing.</li> <li>Mitigation: what we do <em>now</em> to reduce likelihood or impact.</li> <li>Fallback: what we do <em>if it happens</em> - every fallback must preserve a publishable result, even if smaller.</li> <li>Owner: <code>user</code> for actions needing human/lab/supervisor access, <code>agent</code> for repo work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Risk</th> <th>Phase</th> guardrails)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="r-001-supervisor-approval-delayed-or-scope-shifts">R-001: Supervisor approval delayed or scope shifts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (wrong deliverable built).</li> <li>Trigger: Phase 2 implementation slices ready to start (2A-2F complete) with P1-001 still open; or any supervisor communication contradicting <code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code> scope.</li> <li>Status note (2026-07-05): the first trigger fired 2026-06-12 (2A-2F completed with P1-001 still open). The mitigation is holding as designed - all work since has been hardware-independent and harness-shaped (mock slice, docs, Slice 2N is next and is also ungated) - and the fallback (&quot;continue only mock/local work; hardware purchases/borrows blocked-on-approval&quot;) is effectively in force.</li> <li>Mitigation: the queue keeps P1-001 ranked first; all work until approval stays hardware-independent and harness-shaped (valuable under any scope); the Phase 1 exit checklist lists the exact questions to put to the supervisor so one meeting can close the gate.</li> <li>Fallback: if approval stalls past mock-slice completion, continue only mock/local work and mark every hardware purchase or borrow decision blocked-on-approval.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-002-powermetrics-sudo-workflow-not-approved-on-measurement-mac">R-002: powermetrics sudo workflow not approved on measurement Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low (user controls the machine; a local auth session needs rescheduling - the planned 2026-06-10 slot passed without one). Impact: high (no Mac telemetry = no flagship vertical slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with privileged powermetrics capture and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new macOS/MLX/powermetrics versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: scoped sudoers rule (D-004) cannot be installed, or privileged sample capture fails after the auth session.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-004 defines a minimal, single-binary sudoers rule with the exact line documented in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s instrumentation section; interactive-sudo manual fallback documented for attended runs.</li> <li>Fallback: attended runs with interactive sudo (operator present per experiment); if even that is unacceptable, the Mac becomes runtime-supported/telemetry-blocked and the first real slice moves to the first available CUDA target - recorded as a finding, not hidden.</li> <li>Owner: user (install rule), agent (pre-check + structured failure).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-003-mlx-install-or-model-load-failure-on-mac">R-003: MLX install or model-load failure on Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (delays flagship slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with MLX generation and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new MLX/mlx-lm versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: <code>pip install mlx mlx-lm</code> fails, or the chosen model (D-016) has no working MLX artifact.</li> <li>Mitigation: install into a dedicated venv with versions recorded in run bundles; model criteria (D-016) require known MLX availability before selection; smoke-test load before scheduling measurement sessions.</li> <li>Fallback: llama.cpp with the Metal backend as the Mac runtime (already a planned runtime for split portability under D-015); the MLX adapter then becomes optional rather than flagship.</li> <li>Owner: agent (with user approving installs).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-004-kv-persist-resume-unsupported-in-a-target-runtime">R-004: KV persist/resume unsupported in a target runtime</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium overall (high for vLLM file-based replay, low for llama.cpp, low-medium for mlx-lm). Impact: high if unmitigated - this is the project&#39;s central feasibility risk.</li> <li>Trigger: a Stage 3.0 spike returns <code>replay_unsupported</code> for a runtime needed by a planned pairing.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-015&#39;s feasibility ladder - spikes run <em>before</em> any split hardware time is scheduled; pairings are planned only on runtimes with <code>replay_supported</code> verdicts; the synthetic transfer microbenchmark (Stage 3.1) is independent of all runtime cooperation and guarantees a crossover dataset.</li> <li>Fallback: analytical composition - measured prefill energy (node A) + measured synthetic transfer energy (payload sized by the KV model) + measured decode energy (node B) bounds the split cost honestly; the report states the composition method explicitly.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-005-llama-cpp-cache-files-not-portable-across-machines-backends">R-005: llama.cpp cache files not portable across machines/backends</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (session files are version- and model-sensitive; cross-backend CUDA-save -&gt; Metal-load is unverified). Impact: high for <em>heterogeneous</em> pairings specifically.</li> <li>Trigger: Stage 3.0.2&#39;s cross-machine restore test fails or produces divergent output.</li> <li>Mitigation: the spike tests cross-machine restore explicitly, with pinned identical llama.cpp versions and identical GGUF files on both ends, before any heterogeneous experiment is scheduled.</li> <li>Fallback: restrict offline-replay pairings to same-platform pairs (GPU-&gt;GPU in the borrow window, Orin-&gt;Orin); cover heterogeneous pairs with the analytical composition (R-004 fallback); report the portability finding itself - it is a legitimate disaggregation-practicality result.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-006-3080-ti-borrow-window-slips-or-shrinks">R-006: 3080 Ti borrow window slips or shrinks</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (loses GPU-&gt;GPU pairing, not the phase).</li> <li>Trigger: window not scheduled by Phase 3 Stage 3.2 completion; or window arrives before split tooling is ready.</li> <li>Mitigation: all split tooling reaches rehearsed-on-available-hardware state before the window (the Phase 3 plan keeps a borrow-window runbook so borrow time is execution-only, no debugging); calendar mapping task (P1-008) makes the window a tracked date.</li> <li>Fallback: GPU-&gt;GPU pairing drops to single-GPU prefill/decode phase decomposition plus analytical composition; 3050&lt;-&gt;Orin and Orin&lt;-&gt;Orin remain.</li> <li>Owner: user (scheduling), agent (runbook readiness).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-007-no-wall-meter-available">R-007: No wall meter available</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1-4. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (boundary calibration and Pi/Hailo coverage lost; per-target results stand).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-003 resolves &quot;unavailable&quot;.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-003 is a Phase 1 gate precisely so this resolves before it matters; D-018&#39;s boundary table makes results honest without a meter.</li> <li>Fallback: report within-target comparisons (always boundary-consistent) as primary; flag cross-target absolute comparisons with the boundary caveat; targets with no platform telemetry (Pi) become telemetry-unavailable findings.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-008-orin-telemetry-inaccessible">R-008: Orin telemetry inaccessible</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-3. Likelihood: medium (rail sysfs paths vary by L4T version). Impact: low (one target of several).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-006 evidence shows neither INA3221 sysfs nor tegrastats usable.</li> <li>Mitigation: two candidate mechanisms documented before hardware time; wall-meter fallback if R-007 resolves positively.</li> <li>Fallback: Orin runs runtime-only (latency/throughput) marked telemetry-unavailable, or drops to a stretch target.</li> <li>Owner: user (access), agent (adapter).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-009-hailo-cannot-run-llm-shaped-workloads">R-009: Hailo cannot run LLM-shaped workloads</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: high. Impact: low - <em>by design</em>: the plan treats Hailo as a feasibility investigation whose negative verdict is itself a reportable applicability finding.</li> <li>Status: <strong>realized as expected, 2026-06-12</strong> — verdict <code>unsupported_workload</code>. The trigger fired (a non-<code>supported</code> verdict), the by-design mitigation held, and the outcome is the publishable applicability finding the plan anticipated. No schedule impact.</li> <li>Trigger: feasibility checklist closes with any non-<code>supported</code> verdict. (Fired 2026-06-12.)</li> <li>Mitigation: none needed; the verdict-code structure in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s Hailo section makes the outcome publishable either way. Do not spend implementation effort on a Hailo backend (the verdict is now recorded; the standing do-not-do-yet rule becomes &quot;report, don&#39;t implement&quot;).</li> <li>Fallback: Pi 5 CPU-only llama.cpp with wall-meter telemetry becomes an optional low-power data point if the meter exists; otherwise Pi/Hailo appears only in the applicability table.</li> <li>Owner: user (device access), agent (verdict documentation - done).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-010-controller-as-dut-contamination-on-mac-runs">R-010: Controller-as-DUT contamination on Mac runs</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: high if unmitigated. Impact: medium (biased flagship numbers).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-013 (idle baseline includes resident quiescent controller; deferred logging; blocking wait during measured window).</li> <li>Trigger (residual): SSH-controlled comparison runs (once transport exists) show a delta beyond run-to-run variance.</li> <li>Fallback: move Mac headline measurements to remote-controlled runs.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-011-benchmark-network-cannot-be-isolated">R-011: Benchmark network cannot be isolated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (campus/home network constraints unknown until P1-004 closes). Impact: medium (noisy transfer measurements).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-004 topology answer shows shared links only.</li> <li>Mitigation: prefer direct node-to-node cabling (no switch) for 1GbE/2.5GbE point-to-point tests - removes the isolation question entirely for two-node experiments; record link conditions per run in the bundle.</li> <li>Fallback: run sweeps off-hours, repeat n&gt;=5, report observed throughput alongside nominal link speed (the bundle already records measured throughput per D-008&#39;s transfer block).</li> <li>Owner: user (hardware), agent (recording).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-012-schedule-five-phases-vs-fixed-academic-deadlines">R-012: Schedule: five phases vs fixed academic deadlines</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, not by code).</li> <li>Trigger: any phase exceeding its (to-be-set) calendar budget; colloquium or report dates announced (P1-008) leaving less runway than the plan assumes.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-008 maps phases to real dates as soon as the user supplies them (<code>docs/milestones.md</code> holds the skeleton); every phase defines a hardware-independent floor and a descope ladder so cutting is a decision, not a scramble.</li> <li>Descope ladder (worst-case minimum viable capstone, in cut order):<ol> <li>Drop live split (3.3) - already stretch.</li> <li>Drop 10GbE and one model size.</li> <li>Drop heterogeneous replay pairs (keep synthetic transfer + analytical composition).</li> <li>Drop Orin/Pi targets (keep Mac + one CUDA).</li> <li>Floor: mock harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + analytical split model. This is still a complete, defensible benchmark-plus-study.</li> </ol> </li> <li>Owner: user (dates), agent (floor discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-013-thermal-throttling-confounds-measurements">R-013: Thermal throttling confounds measurements</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-4. Likelihood: medium (high on passively-cooled Orin/Pi). Impact: medium (rep-to-rep drift, biased late reps).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-014 (idle-power recovery gate between reps, thermal_drift_c in measurement quality, interleaved ordering) - residual risk on targets without thermal sensors.</li> <li>Trigger: thermal_drift_c trending across reps, or cooldown cap hits recorded in bundles.</li> <li>Fallback: longer cooldowns, active cooling notes recorded in run metadata, or excluding throttled reps <em>with documented cause</em> per D-014.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-014-model-weights-become-unavailable-or-gated">R-014: Model weights become unavailable or gated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (mid-project model swap breaks comparability).</li> <li>Trigger: chosen model&#39;s hub entry gated/removed; license terms change.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-016 requires mirroring chosen weights to local storage immediately on selection, with revisions and hashes recorded.</li> <li>Fallback: promote the recorded fallback candidate; re-run affected baselines (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-015-schema-changes-after-data-collection-starts">R-015: Schema changes after data collection starts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (existing bundles unreadable or silently misread).</li> <li>Status: mitigated structurally.</li> <li>Mitigation: schema_version field exists from v0.1; D-008 plans the only anticipated breaking-shape change (v0.2) <em>before</em> split data collection; output-schema additions are additive-only (the JSON schema does not forbid additional properties); <code>validate-bundle</code> pins what a valid bundle means per version.</li> <li>Trigger: any proposed non-additive change to a schema with bundles already on disk.</li> <li>Fallback: a dated migration note in this repo plus a one-shot migration script; never edit bundles in place (they are evidence).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-016-measurement-corpus-loss-runs-has-no-backup-path">R-016: Measurement-corpus loss (runs/ has no backup path)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-5. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (the dataset behind every claim is a gitignored directory on one disk; a disk failure or an errant delete erases the evidence the defense rests on, and hardware re-collection needs access windows that may not recur).</li> <li>Trigger: first real (non-mock) bundle written; any data-affecting incident (disk error, iCloud eviction anomaly, accidental delete).</li> <li>Mitigation: before the first real measurement session (gate on 2I data collection, tracked as queue task P0-002), define and record the backup protocol here: destination (external disk and/or cloud location outside the repo), cadence (after every measurement session), method (rsync of <code>runs/</code> plus experiment manifests), and a restore test performed once. Configs + manifests already make re-collection well-defined; backups make it unnecessary.</li> <li><strong>Protocol recorded (2026-07-06, P0-002 closed interim).</strong> Destination: <code>~/JouleWise-backup</code> — a user-directed INTERIM location on the same disk (&quot;cursory... I&#39;ll handle that later&quot;); it protects against errant deletes but not disk failure, so the user still owes an external/cloud destination for full mitigation. Cadence: after every measurement session. Method: <code>scripts/backup_runs.sh [RUNS_DIR] [DEST]</code> (rsync -a, never <code>--delete</code>; dated UTC log line per invocation appended to <code>DEST/backup.log</code>). Restore test performed 2026-07-06: mock bundle backed up, restored to a temp dir, <code>validate-bundle</code> green on the restored copy. Swapping in the final destination is a one-argument change (or edit the script default) plus one fresh restore test.</li> <li><strong>Protocol upgraded (2026-07-10/11, P0-003 closed; addendum 2026-07-16 closing a summary-row/body drift found by the resumption audit).</strong> The interim same-disk destination above is superseded: the external destination is iCloud Drive, live with a fresh backup + restore test passed (evidence: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code> §11, &quot;The P0-003 iCloud measurement-corpus backup and restore gate is satisfied&quot;). The 2026-07-06 entry above is retained as history. Standing caveat: iCloud eviction — re-verify the destination is materialized (fresh restore test) before each measurement window.</li> <li>Fallback: re-run affected experiments from their configs (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly per D-005/D-010); report any unrecoverable gap honestly in the exclusion log.</li> <li>Owner: user (destination/media), agent (protocol doc + restore test).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-017-repo-lives-on-icloud-synced-desktop-eperm-lock-recurrence">R-017: Repo lives on iCloud-synced Desktop (EPERM lock recurrence)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: low (mitigated; was high while on Desktop). Impact: medium (blocks work sessions mid-run; small integrity risk around eviction during writes).</li> <li>Status: <strong>mitigated 2026-07-05</strong> - the repo moved off the synced Desktop (current canonical path: <code>~/code/JouleWise</code>; the interim <code>~/code/CapstoneRivoire/Capstone</code> path recorded here was itself later renamed - corrected 2026-07-09, C-027). P0-001 complete; git + suite verified green at the new path. Residual exposure: agent sessions launched from the stale Desktop path (delete the leftover <code>~/Desktop/CapstoneRivoire</code> husk after relaunching from the new path), and any future placement of repo or <code>runs/</code> data under an iCloud-synced directory - do not.</li> <li>Trigger: any <code>Operation not permitted</code> on read/readdir inside the repo with the iCloud file provider (<code>bird</code>) active.</li> <li>History: first incident 2026-06-12 (documented in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>); recurred 2026-07-05 mid-run - <code>docs/</code>, <code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code>, <code>.git</code>, and the repo root EPERM-locked intermittently during an active iCloud full-sync, clearing and re-locking per subtree. Both incidents match iCloud &quot;Optimize Mac Storage&quot; behavior on <code>~/Desktop/</code>. The move landed the same day as the second incident.</li> <li>Fallback: if a lock ever strikes again, wait for it to clear (both incidents did), then re-verify with the test suite before continuing; the remote (<code>origin/main</code>) bounds code loss to the working tree.</li> <li>Owner: user (launch paths), agent (post-lock verification discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-018-the-agent-loop-itself-as-a-schedule-and-scope-risk">R-018: The agent loop itself as a schedule and scope risk</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, R-012).</li> <li>Registered by C-027 (NEGSPACE lens finding accepted in council): the multi-agent workflow can remain locally productive - packs, registries, meta-process, site work - while the graded deliverable path (rubric, report source, backup, real corpus, figures) stays starved. Same-day evidence at registration: ~6M tokens of breadth work vs six real corpus bundles, no report source, same-disk backup.</li> <li>Trigger: an agent-heavy work block that produces neither a new real evidence bundle nor a report/figure increment.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-060 depth-before-breadth stop line (RATIFIED by Ed 2026-07-10) extended by the WO-022/R2 spend guardrails (<code>docs/orchestration.md</code> §Spend guardrails, 2026-07-15); RPT-001 vertical slice; the C-027 correctness rows ranked ahead of all breadth work.</li> <li>Owner: lead (queue discipline + guardrail checkpoints), Ed (HARD bands and structure).</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/risk_register.md · commit dbd8137 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

6d80039</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Measurement Methodology</h1> <p>Living cross-phase contract, drafted in Phase 1. Changes require a decision-log entry when they bind later work.</p> <h2 id="measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</h2> <p>Every benchmark run must be reproducible from its raw artifacts. Summary metrics are derived outputs, not the source of truth.</p> <p>The source of truth for a run is the run bundle:</p> <ul> <li>Experiment config.</li> <li>Device and environment metadata.</li> <li>Event log with phase timestamps.</li> <li>Raw power trace.</li> <li>Raw model output.</li> <li>Reducer output.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry logs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</h2> <p>Before a campaign creates a run bundle, the operator runs the read-only doctor preflight described in <code>docs/contracts/doctor_preflight.md</code>. Schema-0.1 parsing continues to warn-and-ignore unknown keys for compatibility, but campaign execution fails before the first bundle when those warnings have not been explicitly acknowledged. The terminal campaign-verdict JSONL row records the exact warning set and acknowledgement; acknowledgement does not alter config bytes, collection evidence, claim readiness, or claim outcomes.</p> <p>Doctor also exposes architecture/version, configured model and tokenizer identity, requested sampler fields, inspect-only powermetrics privilege policy, thermal pressure, backup capacity, and quiet-machine warnings. These are preflight observations, not substitutes for per-bundle provenance or live measurement gates. In particular, doctor never starts powermetrics and never certifies that a machine is quiet.</p> <h3>Environment guard and per-run admission (D-077)</h3> <p>Campaigns select a strictly typed policy sidecar. <code>run_campaign.py</code> defaults to <code>configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json</code>, records the policy version and exact source-byte SHA-256 in campaign provenance and every member bundle, acquires the campaign lock, and only then performs the enforcing environment preflight before member 1. The production quiet-Mac guard requires AC power and an externally connected power source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Unknown critical probes fail closed. Load averages are recorded as preflight evidence only and never gate a member.</p> <p>Default operation is verify-only. <code>--arm-quiet-mode</code> is an explicit transient operation: the runner displays a countdown, requests <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, and repeats the complete environment probe before deciding admission. It does not write display-sleep, screensaver, or other persistent host settings. An operator override is accepted only when its JSON binds the exact failed snapshot and findings SHA-256 values and records a reason, approver, and timestamp. It is stored as an <code>override</code>, not a waiver, and universally bars all resulting members from gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</p> <p>At each governed member&#39;s idle-baseline stage, the controller captures the same critical environment evidence and verifies that the display remains asleep and the screensaver remains disengaged. Awake, engaged, or unknown state aborts immediately. The first idle baseline is admitted only when the existing powermetrics GPU-idle-quality classification records <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>. One and only one complete retry is allowed; both attempts preserve distinct raw artifacts and provenance. A persistent failure either aborts (production) or records the exploratory-only, unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> claim barrier (<code>on_fail: flag</code>). There is no skip disposition in a fixed-n campaign. A lightweight post-run display/screensaver/HID observation makes within-member transitions visible.</p> <p>The sidecar is deliberately separate from <code>BenchmarkConfig</code>. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy flag-only/non-enforcing behavior, and omission of the additive policy/admission metadata preserves legacy normalized config serialization and hashes.</p> <h3>Per-bundle source provenance</h3> <p><code>RunBundleWriter.create</code> captures the harness source state before it creates bundle artifacts or returns control to any adapter. <code>write_metadata</code> captures the end state after adapter execution. <code>metadata.git_commit</code> remains the creation-time commit for compatibility; the governed record is <code>metadata.source_provenance</code> with schema <code>joulewise.source_provenance.v1</code>.</p> <p>Each <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> snapshot records <code>git_commit</code>, <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, <code>untracked</code>, and <code>diff_sha256</code>. The three state values are independently:</p> <ul> <li><code>clean</code>: the corresponding Git probe succeeded and found no change;</li> <li><code>dirty</code>: an unstaged tracked diff, staged diff, or non-ignored untracked path was present, respectively; or</li> <li><code>unknown</code>: the corresponding probe or required file read failed. Failure is never interpreted as clean.</li> </ul> <p>The privacy-safe diff identity descriptor is <code>sha256</code> / <code>joulewise.git-diff.nul-v1</code>. The producer captures the byte output of <code>git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary</code>, the analogous <code>--cached</code> command, and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z</code>. For each sorted untracked path it hashes, without serializing, the NUL-safe length-framed path, file kind, mode, size, and SHA-256 of regular-file bytes or symlink-target bytes. The final identity is SHA-256 over the version plus length-framed <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, and untracked-inventory byte identities. Bundles contain only the final digest and state labels: never a diff, path, untracked file content, or secret.</p> <p><code>changed_during_run</code> is true when two fully known snapshots differ, false when they match, and null when either snapshot is not fully known. <code>claim_eligible</code> is true only when both commits and diff identities are known, all six component states are clean, and the snapshots match. <code>reason_codes</code> is the deterministic list of every start/end unknown or dirty component followed, when applicable, by <code>source_changed_during_run</code>. Bundle completion remains allowed in every state so raw evidence is not discarded.</p> <p>Dirty, unknown, changed, missing, or internally inconsistent provenance is a hard exclusion for claim-bearing use. The publication pack preflight enforces that boundary and refuses such bundles. Analysis-side admission propagation is separate from capture and field semantics and is owned by WO-004/T11.</p> <ol> <li>Validate config.</li> <li>Create run directory.</li> <li>Collect device metadata.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Warm up runtime.</li> <li>Wait the configured post-warmup settling interval (<code>sampling.warmup_seconds</code>; zero means no wait).</li> <li>Start measured telemetry.</li> <li>Run workload.</li> <li>Stop measured telemetry.</li> <li>Cleanup runtime.</li> <li>Reduce raw artifacts into summary metrics.</li> </ol> <p>The post-warmup settling interval begins only after all active <code>workload_profile.warmup_runs</code> calls and their clock-alignment captures have completed. It ends before the measured-run stage and sampling-active markers, so it is never integrated into the measured window. Controller events record the configured value on the warmup completion event and the runtime log records positive waits.</p> <h2 id="idle-subtraction">Idle Subtraction</h2> <p>Energy metrics must report both gross and idle-subtracted values when possible. The idle baseline is measured before each run and stored in the run bundle.</p> <p>Minimum idle fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle_power_w_mean</code></li> <li><code>idle_power_w_stddev</code></li> <li><code>idle_duration_s</code></li> <li><code>idle_sample_count</code></li> <li><code>telemetry_backend</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="thermal-state">Thermal State</h2> <p>Each telemetry backend should report thermal state before and after measured runs when the platform exposes it.</p> <p>Minimum thermal fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>temperature_c</code></li> <li><code>thermal_pressure</code> or platform equivalent, when available.</li> <li><code>fan_state</code> or cooling mode, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="uncertainty">Uncertainty</h2> <p>Phase 1 defines uncertainty fields; Phase 2 implements reducer behavior. Repeated runs should report:</p> <ul> <li>Number of repetitions.</li> <li>Mean.</li> <li>Standard deviation.</li> <li>Confidence interval method.</li> <li>Confidence interval bounds.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-quality-fields">Measurement Quality Fields</h2> <p>Each run summary should include:</p> <ul> <li>Sampling rate requested.</li> <li>Sampling rate observed.</li> <li>Dropped or malformed samples.</li> <li>Idle variance.</li> <li>Thermal drift.</li> <li>Telemetry source.</li> <li>Local runtime cleanup result (<code>runtime_cleanup_ok</code>: true/false/null). Cleanup occurs after the measured window, so failure is a quality concern for the following repetition and does not retroactively change current-run status or energy.</li> <li>Wall-meter comparison delta, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="phase-labels">Phase Labels</h2> <p>The event log should use stable phase names:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle</code></li> <li><code>warmup</code></li> <li><code>prefill</code></li> <li><code>decode</code></li> <li><code>serialize</code></li> <li><code>transfer</code></li> <li><code>deserialize</code></li> <li><code>cleanup</code></li> <li><code>failure</code></li> </ul> <p><code>deserialize</code> (cache load on the decode node) was added 2026-06-09 alongside the split-run accounting definitions (see <code>docs/phase_3/phase_3_plan.md</code>); phase labels are strings in the schema, so the addition is non-breaking. Split-stage accounting, pinned so reducers and prose agree: serialize = cache-persist window on the prefill node; transfer = byte-movement window; deserialize = cache-load window on the decode node; decode = first-token to last-token. Cache load is not decode energy.</p> <h2 id="hardware-classification">Hardware Classification</h2> <p>Every target should end Phase 1 in one state:</p> <ul> <li><code>supported</code>: known viable and ready for Phase 2 implementation.</li> <li><code>pending</code>: expected viable but not fully checked.</li> <li><code>unsupported</code>: not viable for a documented technical reason.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-boundaries">Measurement Boundaries</h2> <p>&quot;Power&quot; means a different physical boundary on each telemetry backend. Cross-target absolute comparisons must state the boundary difference; the final report&#39;s limitations section inherits this table. Decision D-018 defines the rail policy (per-rail trace rows plus a per-backend rail manifest naming the canonical sum).</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backend</th> <th>Boundary</th> <th>Included</th> <th>Excluded</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>powermetrics</td> <td>Apple SoC subsystems</td> <td>CPU + GPU + ANE package power</td> <td>display, storage, memory at wall, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_smi</td> <td>GPU board</td> <td>board power as reported by driver</td> <td>host CPU, DRAM, motherboard, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>jetson_rails</td> <td>module input (VDD_IN preferred; actual rail recorded)</td> <td>module power</td> <td>carrier-board peripherals (rail-dependent), PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>wall_meter</td> <td>full system AC</td> <td>everything incl. PSU losses</td> <td>nothing</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mock</td> <td>synthetic</td> <td>n/a</td> <td>n/a</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Rules:</p> <ul> <li>Within-target comparisons (the same backend) are always boundary-consistent and are the primary claim type.</li> <li>Cross-target comparisons are reported with boundaries named; where the wall meter exists, the wall-vs-platform delta is recorded per target and used to contextualize the gap.</li> <li>Each telemetry adapter declares its rail manifest in <code>device_metadata</code>; the reducer sums exactly the manifest rails to produce <code>power_w</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="clock-synchronization-and-multi-node-alignment">Clock Synchronization And Multi-Node Alignment</h2> <p>Policy per decision D-003:</p> <ul> <li>Canonical <code>timestamp_s</code> everywhere is epoch UTC from <code>time.time()</code> via the injected clock; no other time base appears in artifacts.</li> <li>Each process records its monotonic-vs-wall offset at start in metadata (detects wall-clock steps mid-run).</li> <li>Each node records NTP sync state in metadata when determinable.</li> <li>For multi-node runs, the controller bounds per-node clock offset with marker events: timestamp a no-op command on the remote node immediately before and after each remote stage; half the round trip bounds the offset. The bound is recorded in composite-bundle metadata.</li> <li>Reducers must flag (in measurement quality) any cross-node interval shorter than the recorded offset bound; such intervals are not used for energy attribution claims.</li> <li>Required precision: at 1-10 Hz power sampling, tens of milliseconds - comfortably within LAN NTP plus the marker bound.</li> </ul> <h2 id="controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</h2> <p>On Mac-local runs the controller process runs on the measured machine. Mitigation per decision D-013:</p> <ul> <li>The idle baseline is measured with the controller resident and quiescent, so the controller&#39;s floor load is included in what idle subtraction removes.</li> <li>During the measured window the controller only blocks on the runtime: no logging, no polling, no file writes; log records buffer in memory and flush after sampling stops.</li> <li>Residual risk is recorded, not hidden: OS background activity affects idle and measured windows alike; the upgrade path (remote-controlled Mac runs once the SSH transport exists) is queued as a validation comparison.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, Ordering, And Thermal Equilibrium</h2> <p>Per decisions D-005 and D-014:</p> <ul> <li>Each repetition is an independent run bundle; an experiment manifest groups members and records the executed order.</li> <li>Between live repetitions, cooldown v2 holds until the retained evidence has both a complete 30-second wall-clock span and at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code> of captured coverage (<code>coverage_fraction = 0.8</code> by default), and its duration-weighted idle-power mean satisfies the one-sided rule <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code> (10% by the production policy), while thermal pressure is Nominal. A below-reference mean therefore counts as recovery. An optional calibrated absolute ceiling is an additional upper cap and never an OR escape. The wait has a 5-minute cap; the cap is evaluated before release on every iteration, so recovery criteria first met at or after the deadline remain a <code>cap_hit</code> (with the late criteria recorded in the trace) and are recorded in the following repetition&#39;s measurement quality.</li> <li>The preceding baseline is eligible as a cooldown reference only when <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>, all critical environment probes passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. An ineligible or unknown reference falls back to one frozen clean anchor: the NEG-8 reference start when present, otherwise the first admission-passing baseline. The anchor&#39;s source and hashes are recorded and it is never updated from later outcomes. With neither an eligible reference nor an anchor the gate fails closed. The following member records policy version, eligibility decision, anchor provenance, thresholds (including <code>coverage_fraction</code>), wall-clock span, required and observed coverage, thermal result, and the exact release criterion under <code>preceding_campaign_cooldown</code>. Historical recovered rows retain their recorded meaning and are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>Conditions are interleaved round-robin where model-reload cost permits; where blocks are operationally forced, the order is recorded so drift correlation can be audited (Phase 4 Stage 4.5 does this audit).</li> </ul> <h2 id="statistical-protocol">Statistical Protocol</h2> <p>Per decision D-014 (draft to be ratified against observed variance at Phase 4 Stage 4.0), amended 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3; amendments ratified by D-053):</p> <ul> <li>Repetitions: n &gt;= 5 for headline comparisons; n &gt;= 3 minimum elsewhere; the n is recorded per experiment.</li> <li>Intervals: report mean, sample standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval via Student t; Phase 4 runs a bootstrap sensitivity comparison and reports both where they materially disagree.</li> <li>Outliers: flagged by modified z-score on MAD &gt; 3.5; never silently dropped; reported with-and-without only when a physical cause is identified and documented; otherwise kept in headline numbers. Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): at n &lt;= 10, reports also run a leave-one-out influence check on every claim-bearing contrast. The report lists the full-data estimate/CI/verdict and each leave-one-out estimate/CI/verdict. An omitted point is influential if it changes the sign, floor status, adjusted rejection/equivalence verdict, or moves the estimate by more than 0.25 x the active threshold: MDE for rank/MDE-gated claims, otherwise the floor gate. Influential points are reported as sensitivity evidence, not silently removed.</li> <li>Figures always show raw points alongside aggregates.</li> <li>Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): differences are claimed from the confidence interval of the paired/block difference, or from the named model contrast, not by visual separation of marginal intervals. Where execution order was randomized, the analysis includes a permutation/randomization check for the same contrast following the actual randomization scheme, permuting labels only within exchangeable blocks/strata. The minimum for this check is 6 exchangeable blocks; below that count, report the check as not run and rely on the contrast CI with the caveat that randomization-inference sensitivity was underpowered. A paired contrast is preferred when it matches the design; mixed or hierarchical models are reserved for real dependence structures that a paired/block contrast cannot represent. Floor-gated outcomes use a three-way rule: below-floor contrasts are <code>not resolvable</code>; above-floor contrasts whose CI does not support direction are <code>unresolved</code> with no directional claim; equivalence or &quot;no difference&quot; language requires a predeclared equivalence gate whose margin exceeds the floor and whose contrast CI lies entirely within that margin.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
