Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-file">docs/<wbr>council_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<h1>JouleWise: Project Status, Plan, And Architecture</h1> <p>Audience: project advisor. This is the standalone monitoring document - it summarizes what the project is, how it is built, where it stands, and what it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository are provided for anyone who wants the full evidence trail.</p> <ul> <li>Freshness owner: phase completion lives in the phase exit checklists; live gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>; the canonical suite command and CI own the current verification result. This page deliberately does not duplicate volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.</li> <li>Repository state: <code>main</code> contains the repaired measurement instrument (D-078 phase 0) and the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10; council C-033). The repaired-instrument collection has 229 members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are useful diagnostic evidence that the instrument works, but they are not claim-bearing and do not yet publish a floor. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine collection following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>; if it passes, it will produce the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</li> <li>Project phase: see the phase exit checklists for exact completion state; live eligibility and next work come from the generated state kernel, not this reader-facing summary.</li> <li>Repository: <code>github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</code> (branch <code>main</code>)</li> <li>Live status site: <a href="https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app">https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app</a> (Lakebed capsule; it is an Ed-deployed snapshot, not the repository authority. <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code> records known differences; agents refresh that report when front-facing state changes and never regenerate or deploy the site.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="current-repository-view-30-second-read">Current Repository View — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The repaired instrument has completed its first collection era, but the first claim-grade floor is still ahead.</strong> The D-078 phase-0 repair fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22. Four bracketed windows then collected 229 strict members (a5-a8). They are retained as non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence: they showed that the repaired path works and exposed the remaining drift-screen problem, but they are not a published floor set.</p> <p>That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims. The next quiet session will mint its bound inside the window and collect three start references, one midpoint reference, and three end references. The older 222-bundle floor table below remains visible as a caveated historical record, not the current measurement posture.</p> <p>AXI-SB remains <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.</p> <h3>Published Window-A floor summary</h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>CAVEAT (2026-07-19 soundness audit):</strong> a trace-time-anchor defect was found in the powermetrics evidence path (power timestamps misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale). It affects the corpora behind this table; every row below is <strong>under re-adjudication</strong> and none should be cited as a promoted floor until the instrument is repaired and the rows re-extracted. Record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> </blockquote> <p>Every energy value below is a false-effect guard floor in joules on the <strong>Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary (CPU + GPU + ANE)</strong>. Gross is the D-067 headline basis; idle-subtracted values are labeled within-device secondary views. Absolute rows use repeated identical conditions; comparative rows use same-condition ABBA blocks. Each primary row uses <code>n=10</code> strict-valid bundles or ABBA blocks.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>window / basis</th> <th align="right">absolute floor</th> <th align="right">comparative floor</th> <th align="right">computed <code>floor_gate_j</code> / disposition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>mid request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.527 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mid request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.537 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.052 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.059 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>prefill phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.477 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>decode phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.786 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short-prefill stress, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.027 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">smoke-only; <code>not_resolvable_sample_count</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite item, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.333 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J; drift review required</td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite level, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.664 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J; drift review required</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>The start/end NEG-8 reference pair is an <code>n=2</code> drift diagnostic, not a campaign floor. Its gross request energy moved by 7.659 J; the idle-subtracted within-device secondary view moved by 6.608 J (same boundary). Verified extraction: <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json</code>; reader deliverable: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-17-window-a-brief.html</code>.</p> <h3>2026-07-19 re-calibration under the environment guard — PRELIMINARY</h3> <p>The caveated suite rows were re-measured in two bracketed windows under the D-077 guard: <strong>94 strict-valid bundles</strong>, all admission predicates satisfied. Reviewed readout: suite gross <strong>147.96 ± 0.39 J</strong> clean (contaminated cells were ~+30%); frozen-estimator provisional comparative floor <strong>≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%)</strong> from 5 of 10 planned ABBA blocks (~22× tighter, same estimator, than the caveated figure); long-decode <strong>83.9 mJ/output-token</strong>, matching the 07-17 decode cell to ~0.1%. That corpus was claim-ineligible on source provenance (dirty collection tree); details: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html</code>.</p> <p>UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid bundles with clean source provenance (<code>runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/</code>) cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n, including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source provenance gate is closed. <strong>SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.</strong> In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to ~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the workload&#39;s start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for sub-second test runs (one 0.37 s run read 0.27 J when its true consumption, plainly present in the recording, was <del>8 J), and a meaningful hidden uncertainty (</del>±10 J) even on 60-second runs. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply below this instrument&#39;s resolution and will not be claimed — by design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter&#39;s own timestamps, attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md</code>; technical record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and signed off.</strong> Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened relative to the model&#39;s work (the clock-alignment fix, with the alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with, mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is automatically rejected; and (c) refuses to report a result rather than report a doubtful one, in every failure case we could construct. One known limitation is recorded honestly: the file that stores the detection-floor statistics is not yet cryptographically tied back to the raw measurements it came from, so we only trust such files when our own pipeline produced them in the same verified session (a fix is queued). Live validation on the real hardware passed: the validation recording (made under the earlier 40-pulse calibration procedure) detected all 40 calibration pulses with no false detections, and a test measurement reproduced the expected physics where the old defective pipeline had been wrong by a factor of ~28. Production measurements will use the newer 59-pulse calibration procedure, which supports the stronger statistical guarantee we quote for the timing error bar. Next: a fresh calibration and re-collection of the measurement campaign under the repaired instrument. Record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-20-p0-instrument-repair.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>COLLECTION ERA UPDATE (2026-07-24): the repaired instrument has now been proven in production.</strong> Over two nights we collected 229 clean measurements across four properly-bracketed windows. The standout result: two identical reference measurements taken three hours apart agreed to within 0.007 joules on a ~38.5 joule task — about 0.02%, which is excellent repeatability for whole-system power measurement. The windows are not yet &quot;claim-grade&quot; for one honest reason: our own stability check (comparing a reference task at each window&#39;s start and end) was found to be asking a mathematically unanswerable question, so it failed every window on a technicality while the underlying data was good. After a formal debate between the two AI models working on the project — which the reviewing model won on one substantive point — the check was redesigned and ratified: windows are now screened for anomalous drift against a limit derived from measured repeatability (instead of an arbitrary constant), and any drift observed is carried into the results&#39; error bars rather than being ignored once a window &quot;passes&quot;. Reference measurements are also being tripled at each window edge. One collection session under the new rules produces the project&#39;s first claim-grade detection-floor table, which then sizes the Splitwise replication experiments. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-23-window-a-collection-arc.md</code>, decision log D-078 clauses 8-10.</p> <p><strong>SCREENING RULES BUILT, AUDITED, AND MERGED (2026-07-25; council C-033).</strong> The redesigned stability screen described above is now implemented and on main: both energy families are screened separately, every passing window carries an explicit drift allowance into its error bars, drift limits expire after 24 hours so stale calibrations cannot be reused, and a measurement whose internal clock had to be guessed can never anchor a result (that one rule alone corrected a floor that was overstated by roughly a factor of three). The code went through an unusually deep adversarial review — four independent audit rounds and three rounds of cross-examination between two different AI models — which caught and fixed several ways the new rules could have been silently bypassed. The step-by-step measurement procedure for the next collection session is written up in <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-24-screen-budget-gauntlet.md</code>, council log C-033.</p> <h3>Exploratory follow-on — not a promoted claim</h3> <p>Nine additional strict-valid, collection-usable bundles cover three repetitions each of unmatched OLMoE-1B-7B BF16, Qwen3-4B INT4, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4 configurations on the fixed five-item <code>jw_mixed_v1_sentinel</code> shape. Every bundle is claim-evidence-flagged, the model/config points differ in architecture, scale, tokenizer, and quantization, and the repetition count is below the headline protocol. The values are therefore descriptive <strong>EXPLORATORY / L1-legacy observations only</strong>.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J (227.141–231.790 J)</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token (177.454–181.086 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s (122.261–122.481 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J (362.642–362.903 J)</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token (283.314–283.518 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s (106.470–106.545 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J (1061.722–1085.144 J)</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token (829.471–847.769 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s (39.349–39.569 tok/s)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Each bundle emitted 1,280 generated output tokens. Gross per-output-token values above are derived from the gross suite numerator; the stored <code>energy_output_token_j</code> field instead uses the idle-subtracted numerator and is retained as a labeled within-device secondary view in the full extraction. For the like-for-like suite-level gross window on the Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary, the exploratory OLMoE-versus-Qwen3-4B mean gap is 133.720 J, above the published 24.619 J suite-level gross <code>floor_gate_j</code>. That only says the descriptive gap exceeds the measurement guard: unmatched configurations, evidence flags, drift review, and the lack of a prospective contrast still prohibit efficiency or architecture claims. Every aggregate and raw repetition is bundle-cited in <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-c-027-whole-project-council-review-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, C-027 whole-project council review) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The project put itself in front of a hostile examiner and corrected its own front page.</strong> A seven-lens cross-model review (new Codex model, extra-high reasoning) plus an independent final examiner audited the docs, the scientific claims, the statistics implementation, the architecture, and the operating loop itself. Verdict: the evidence discipline and instrument core are sound, but reader-facing claims had drifted from the evidence (the 1.5B per-token headline used the wrong denominator — now corrected as <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~79-90 mJ per generated output token), the D-053 contrast-CI machinery exists as binding specs but not yet as code (now owned as queue rows P2-037..P2-042 and gating Window-A interpretation), and the loop&#39;s own audit trail and the capstone-critical path (grading rubric, report skeleton, off-machine backup, one data-to-figure slice) need attention before any new breadth. All measured values above remain legacy L1 preliminary observations. Full adjudicated record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-09-c027-whole-project-review.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-advisor-status-cockpit-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, advisor status cockpit) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The public preview is being upgraded for live advisor observation.</strong> The project-status page remains generated from repository evidence, but Lakebed now has a narrow fail-soft live overlay contract: freshness from GitHub commit checks plus parsed current fields from <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>, <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>, and the risk register. The advisor cockpit adds live snapshot state, attention items, campaign readiness, evidence cards, and claim-ceiling panels; the Story page drops hand-authored volatile counts. The operational policy is D-051: repo markdown remains the source of truth and Lakebed never hides static provenance. Current work follows <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>: C-019 shakedown, then P2-015 quiet calibration for Window A (the CP-5 stop card was cleared 2026-07-09).</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-08-all-four-streams-merged-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-08, all four streams merged) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>Everything landed.</strong> The multi-stream session merged as four PRs: P2-013 and P2-014 are closed — all 31 audit pins fixed, the suite passed with zero expected failures (current count authority is RUN_STATE.md Current Verification; the suite-build merge was 732 tests and the post-alignment state is 734), bundle provenance now records prompt/workload identities, and <code>validate-bundle --strict</code> includes the powermetrics raw-plist-to-trace gate plus the legacy additive-summary comparison. The six existing real corpus bundles pass strict read-only and unrewritten; strict proves re-derivation of the recorded evidence, not independent rerunning of the hardware session. New-era bundles must carry shape-valid provenance to pass. The Stage 3.0.1 KV spike is merged with a lead-reverified verdict of <code>replay_supported</code> (tokens identical; cache size +0.018% vs prediction) — Phase 3&#39;s central technical risk is retired on current hardware. The fixture-first 2K NVIDIA stack is merged; ALL its protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until first live hardware contact (the live-verification checklist is ready). The independent project critique now carries a second-pass reassessment (its recommendations that became code are marked resolved; 16/17 of its checkable claims were lead-verified against file evidence): <code>docs/project_critique_review.html</code>. Next: the detection-floor calibration (P2-015) then the 2M two-model baseline campaign on a quiet machine. Reader-facing status below defers to the phase checklist matrix rows for per-item authority.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fifth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fifth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The instrument grew four capabilities in one session and is now campaign-ready.</strong> <em>(Historical claim; C-027 (2026-07-09) supersedes the gating: execution is conditioned on P0-003 backup, P2-038, P2-039, and P2-015-SMOKE.)</em> Five parallel work streams landed (PRs #2-#6): (1) <strong>statistical uncertainty</strong> — every multi-repetition experiment now carries per-metric 95% confidence intervals with outlier detection and explicit below-protocol flags, re-derivable byte-identically from the raw evidence bundles (verified on a live 3-repetition run as <strong>D-014 verification workload, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> 99.19 ± 1.36 mJ/output-token); (2) <strong>contamination detection</strong> — an idle-window quality gate that mechanically flags runs taken on a non-quiet machine (it caught its first real contamination during verification); (3) <strong>deep telemetry</strong> — per-sample GPU/CPU-cluster frequency and residency forensics plus a machine-state snapshot in every bundle; (4) <strong>campaign automation</strong> — a deterministic config-matrix generator and a resumable sequential runner, so the planned two-model baseline matrix (4 workload shapes × 2 models × 5 repetitions) runs unattended. A review council also produced a hardware-tiered research agenda: 16 questions answerable on current hardware alone, 10 more behind planned gates (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The P2-013 evidence-integrity and P2-014 provenance fixes are now complete; next Mac corpus step is the baseline matrix on a quiet machine.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fourth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fourth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>A flagship-class model is now benchmarked.</strong> Qwen3.5-122B (Feb 2026 generation, 122B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 10B active, a reasoning model) ran through the identical harness and workload on the M3 Max. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. Throughput was 46 tokens/s, and the gross-energy sample CV was 0.3% across three sequential repetitions in one warm-cache session. The earlier model recorded <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per request and <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~87 mJ per generated output token at 257 tok/s. <em>(Metric bases and CV wording corrected 2026-07-09, C-027.)</em> First cross-model finding: the two measured points differ in size, architecture, and quantization, so they are not a demonstrated scaling law. They are, however, consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal structure Q4 models: <strong>unsubtracted decode-window mean power — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~23.5 W for P2-003 and ~27.5 W for FLAGSHIP-001, while the bigger model&#39;s cost showed up mostly as time. Also this update: the research agenda grew to six named questions (Q4-Q6) after a multi-model review council, with a curated question bank (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>) and an instrument roadmap (richer telemetry parsing, a difficulty-graded scored workload suite, and implementing the statistical-uncertainty protocol) queued.</p> <h2 id="update-ledger">Update Ledger</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>date</th> <th>label</th> <th>one-line outcome</th> <th>run-report link</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Measurement-soundness audit (Ed-directed)</td> <td>VERDICT: unsound for claim-bearing use as recorded — trace-time-anchor defect misattributes request/phase energies (all four P0s lead-verified); metric-level prechecks already failed 238/288 request metrics; four cooldown cap hits unjoined; analysis-engine wire incompat. docs/process_traces/2026-08-04-quiet-guard-spec/IMPL-PACKET.md:203:**Not run by this packet or by any implementation agent session.** After Commit 3 is gauntlet-clean, Ed/lead creates a quiet, zero-agent session and predeclares Q8's numeric threshold before inspecting outcomes. Run one matched **A/B/B/A** round where A is the watcher absent and B is the exact production watcher blocked in `waitpid`; T3 stays down. Each capture records raw powermetrics, whole-system power/energy, watcher user/system CPU time, maximum RSS, context switches, and wakeups where available. Report the watcher-present minus watcher-absent estimate and its 95% upper bound against Ed's threshold. Custody is permanently NON-CLAIM and disjoint from claim runs, baselines, calibration, and NEG-8. Passing licenses the characterized watcher version/runtime/OS/hardware tuple; failure means redesign/recharacterize or abandon, never subtract. Repeat after material watcher code/interpreter behavior, OS, or hardware changes.

## Current Repository View — 30-second read

**The repaired measurement path has produced its first floor artifact, but
that artifact is not currently claim-bearing.** The D-078 phase-0 repair
fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22; the drift-screen
rules merged on 2026-07-25; the first fully clean measurement windows
passed on 2026-07-25/26, and on 2026-07-30 the project minted its first
floor artifact from them. D-110 later made that mint non-claim-bearing
pending governed re-derivation and remint. A second calibration window
(the 7B model) passed overnight on 2026-07-29, surviving two
live contamination events that the admission gates caught and recovered
from per the written playbook. The earlier a5-a8 windows (229 members)
remain non-claim-bearing, instrument-proving evidence.

**The head-to-head comparison ran on 2026-07-30→31 and passed every
collection and whole-window gate.** Comparing the small (1.5B) and large (7B)
model decoding the same text, the large model used **about 147 J (whole-request, idle-subtracted — a diagnostic view; the registered per-phase comparison metric gives 141.29 J) more energy per response**
— and the run-to-run scatter of that difference across ten paired blocks
was only about **0.24 J**, roughly six hundred times smaller than the
effect. This is the kind of demonstration the metrology framing calls for: a
real effect the instrument resolves with enormous margin, measured under
frozen, pre-registered rules. (Preliminary observation from the raw
per-run summaries. The comparison's bookkeeping schema landed on
2026-08-02, but D-110 blocks formal consumption until the calibration
campaign on a quiet machine. Reader-facing status below defers to the
phase checklist matrix rows for per-item authority.

corpora</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-19. Owner: lead session under Ed&#39;s soundness-audit directive; recorded so the gate binds future sessions immediately. Status update 2026-07-22: the gate has been operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the entire repair arc, and Ed explicitly ratified the close-out cap (clause 8); formal ratification of this original text rides the PR #79 review (Ed may amend).</p> <p>The 2026-07-19 measurement-soundness audit (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>; all P0 findings lead-verified from primary evidence) found that powermetrics trace timestamps are misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale (pre-spawn/first-parse midpoint anchor), making request/phase/item point energies physically non-attributable as recorded across ALL existing powermetrics corpora, including the 2026-07-17 published floor extraction.</p> <p>Binding until amended:</p> <ol> <li>No claim-bearing floor, MDE, or L2/L3 energy claim may be published from any corpus collected under the defective anchor. Existing corpora are instrument/calibration evidence only.</li> <li>Extraction must treat <code>window_evidence_precheck</code> as a hard gate and must join campaign-log cooldown/admission evidence (cap hits are not clean n). &quot;Claim-eligible&quot; narrative language may describe METRIC-level eligibility only, never source provenance alone.</li> <li>The repair path (roadmap Phase 0, <code>docs/phase_2/splitwise_replication_roadmap.md</code>): tight causal anchor + anchor-shift joule envelope in reduction, analysis-engine 0.5.0/v2 wire compat, CPU-aware idle admission, prospective NEG-8 acceptance threshold. Stored summaries are never rewritten; fixes are prospective.</li> <li>The 2026-07-17 published floor table is caveated in PROJECT_STATUS pending re-extraction; advisor-brief/site correction timing is Ed&#39;s deployment decision (D-068).</li> </ol> <p>Revisit trigger: Phase 0 repair lands with live pulse-validation evidence, or Ed rules a different salvage/disposition for existing corpora.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-20: fail-closed vocabulary and immutable summaries</h3> <p>Additive amendment under the adversarial soundness fix round. These additions only refuse or widen uncertainty; none can license a claim.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21: convergence fix wave (lead adjudications)</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the two-round cross-model convergence loop over <code>impl/p0-instrument-repair</code> (round-2 and round-3 fix waves; council log carries the layer accounting). Six rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Additive causal-bound composition.</strong> <code>B_effective = B_bundle + B_fiducial</code> replaces <code>max(B_bundle, B_fiducial)</code>.
