The prior <code>max()</code> text in this log is superseded prospectively; stored summaries are never rewritten.</li> <li><strong>Identity bump, not in-place semantics change.</strong> The additive composition, fiducial protocol_v2 physics (<code>joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2</code> full 2-D branch-and-bound region), and the stricter evidence-admission semantics are minted as reducer <code>0.5.2</code> / AXI <code>0.6.2</code> with <code>configs/calibration/powermetrics_fiducial/protocol_v2.json</code>. <code>0.5.1</code> / <code>0.6.1</code> and <code>protocol_v1.json</code> remain byte-frozen replay arms.</li> <li><strong>Superseded arms are claim-ineligible.</strong> <code>0.5.1</code>/<code>0.6.1</code> summaries refuse claim-bearing use with a registered refusal (superseded max-composition envelope semantics); <code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code> are the sole claim-eligible mints.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions (closing the F11/PENDING exception).</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>token_count_stream_chunk_fallback</code> (renamed from the source-label reuse of <code>stream_chunk_fallback</code>), <code>pulse_calibration_rollover_gate_timeout</code> (pre-workload rollover gate timeout now refuses fail-closed, no artifact minting), and <code>post_window_trace_tail_shorter_than_anchor_bound</code> (reduce-time refusal when the post-window trace tail cannot support the composed anchor bound; collection policy raises the minimum post-window dwell to 1.0 s). These only refuse; none can license a claim.</li> <li><strong>Registry closure is one-way by design.</strong> Every emitted spelling must be registered here; a registered spelling with no current emission site (e.g. <code>window_evidence_precheck_failed</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>) is permitted — unemittable names cannot launder anything.</li> <li><strong>Member-level <code>claim_evidence_flags</code> is an all-leaf union — documented, not changed.</strong> Adjudicated a documentation defect only: the union is fail-safe (it can only over-flag, never over-admit) and gating decisions read the per-metric leaves. Scope documented in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>; no wire rename.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (second): two-edge envelope and confirmation-round rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the first confirmation round over <code>5093355</code> correctly withheld sign-off (fresh Sol xhigh audit; 8 confirmed findings, one P0). Rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Corner-composed two-edge envelope (P0 repair).</strong> The calibration fits independent start-edge and stop-edge emission lags; a single common trace shift under-covers because independent endpoint errors move energy by up to <code>2·P·B_fiducial</code> even when a common shift cancels. The claim envelope is now the extrema over start = <code>delta_common + eps_on</code>, stop = <code>delta_common + eps_off</code> with <code>|delta_common| &lt;= B_bundle</code> and <code>|eps_on|, |eps_off| &lt;= B_fiducial</code> independent. For nonnegative power the energy is monotone in each edge separately, so exact extrema are attained at the four edge corners with the common shift scanned continuously — the existing breakpoint-exact scan run per corner. The per-edge corner offset is <code>±(B_fiducial + wall_minus_monotonic_span)</code>: the span is a third disjoint per-edge error source, folded into the corners (delta-review amendment) rather than the frozen arms&#39; cruder <code>2·span·maxP</code> additive term, and the composed <code>anchor_bound_s</code> = <code>B_bundle + B_fiducial + span</code> governs the tail-sufficiency gate identically. Idle-subtracted and per-token envelopes additionally widen by <code>2·(B_fiducial + span)·P_idle</code> because independent edges vary the subtracted idle duration (delta re-audit catch). New registered method spelling for the 0.5.2/0.6.2 mints; v1/v2 spellings remain replay-read-only.</li> <li><strong>In-place revision of the unreleased mints.</strong> Reducer 0.5.2 / AXI 0.6.2 were never merged or used for stored artifacts; their envelope semantics are revised in place (no 0.5.3/0.6.3 inflation). Goldens regenerated and hand-verified against the formula.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions.</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>negative_power_sample</code> (negative rail power reaching the envelope/energy path breaks the monotonicity argument and refuses fail-closed) and <code>instrument_calibration_stale</code> (calibration artifacts now record capture wall time and a 24 h <code>max_age_s</code> validity horizon in protocol_v2; claim-time verification refuses missing/invalid capture time or age exceeded — a finite 40-pulse residual maximum is not an out-of-sample bound without recency enforcement). Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>capture_time_missing_or_invalid</code> (a v2 capture without a valid recorded capture wall time is invalid at minting, with the reason stated rather than silent). All only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception is retired with this entry. Replay purity note: the 0.5.1/0.6.1 arms keep their frozen binding expectation against the protocol_v2.json bytes current at their mint (<code>REPLAY_PROTOCOL_V2_SHA256</code>); custody-manifest verification and the staleness horizon are current-mint gates only.</li> <li><strong>Environment admission consumes the full evidence object.</strong> The shared validator fails closed on <code>critical_environment_passed</code>, <code>reference_provenance_present</code>, per-run evaluation eligibility, guard observations, and schema identity — and the post-run environment observation passes through the failure predicate on claim/whole-window paths (a post-run critical-environment failure refuses claim eligibility). This closes the Window-A screensaver contamination class end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>Calibration custody verified at claim time.</strong> The reducer enforces the validation-manifest reference: in-bundle containment, manifest hash, and presence + sha256 of every manifest member; any failure refuses as <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>. Current-era (0.5.2/0.6.2) claim-bearing use requires a protocol_v2 calibration artifact.</li> <li><strong>Collection floors.</strong> The 1.0 s post-window dwell minimum is enforced on every collection path (controller default, schema minimum, campaign-policy validation); sub-minimum configs refuse at validation. Scope spelling (delta-review adjudication): controller/CLI pre-collection rejection applies wherever powermetrics telemetry collects; mock-backend runs are not dwell-gated at the controller (mock telemetry cannot reach any claim path), while the campaign-policy schema minimum applies universally. Inner phase/item/block/level window entries carry the whole-trace anchor/calibration/tail barrier stamps whenever the top-level barrier fires.</li> <li><strong>Cooldown terminal-evidence normativity documented.</strong> The required terminal JSONL row fields (<code>release</code>, <code>release_criteria_met_late</code>), the cap-first precedence rule (&quot;the cap is causal and wins&quot;), and rejection semantics are contract text in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>, matching <code>joulewise/cooldown.py</code> exactly.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (third): provenance authentication rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after confirmation round 2 over <code>233e9e3</code> withheld sign-off (9 confirmed; the physics verified clean from every lens — all findings are provenance/governance). Rulings, implemented in the round-3 fix wave (frozen 0.5.1/0.6.1 replay semantics unchanged throughout):</p> <ol> <li><strong>Declared facts are authenticated against primary bytes.</strong> The calibration&#39;s declared <code>capture_wall_time_s</code> must agree (±1 s) with the capture time independently derived from the hash-verified source events — a stale calibration can no longer be relabeled fresh (the P0).</li> <li><strong>Freshness covers the whole measurement.</strong> The 24 h horizon binds both <code>run_started</code> and the measured window END: <code>capture &lt;= run_started</code> and <code>window_end &lt;= capture + max_age_s</code>, inclusive. Pre-run delays cannot carry sampling past the declared validity of its calibration.</li> <li><strong>Version identity is validated generically.</strong> Generic bundle validation checks <code>reducer_version</code> against the closed known set and the §8.1 version/event-semantics pairing rules as a validation-time structured problem (no wire-schema enum — frozen-arm byte replay preserved); an unsupported <code>--reducer-version</code> yields the standard structured refusal, never a traceback.</li> <li><strong>Stored verdicts are re-derived, never trusted.</strong> The whole-window verifier rejects duplicated NEG-8 core members (occurrence-count semantics) and re-derives the bracket verdict from member evidence; disagreement with the stored row is <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Delta-review strengthening (lead ruling): the re-derivation tolerances come from the repo-REGISTERED campaign policy whose file hash matches the row&#39;s <code>policy_sha256</code> — the one trust anchor that does not terminate at bundle custody. Unknown policy hashes, and rows whose self-asserted tolerances disagree with the registered policy, refuse <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> before re-derivation. The custody boundary is otherwise explicit: a forger with bundle write access can rewrite row-internal hashes consistently, but cannot mint a matching tracked policy file.</li> <li><strong>Protocol identity is shape-authenticated.</strong> A v2 <code>protocol_id</code> requires the v2 estimator identity, capture/horizon fields, and v2 residual shape; v1-shaped bodies relabeled v2 refuse <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li><strong>Admission attempts have timing semantics.</strong> Attempt-ledger rows carry strictly increasing, non-overlapping declared windows on the strict path; violations refuse <code>environment_admission_missing</code>. 7a. <strong>(Fourth-wave addendum — claim-aggregation rulings, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 3 over <code>0925480</code> (instrument core verified defensible on fresh head collections by every lens; all four P0s in the claim-aggregation layer), the lead ruled: (1) floors/MDEs widen by EXACT linear-corner evaluation over member envelope intervals — residual widening <code>w_i·(n−1)/n + Σ_{j≠i}w_j/n</code>, contrast widening <code>Σ|c_i|·w_i</code> — never a max-width shortcut, and the dominance refusal fires against the widened quantity; (2) admission is causally bound to its run: the final attempt window ends at-or-before window start within <code>MAX_ADMISSION_GAP_S = 600</code> (inclusive), the post-run observation is captured at-or-after window end, and attempt windows must contain their stage&#39;s recorded idle-capture interval; (3) the whole-window verifier re-derives CPU admission and adapter continuity from member-bundle primary evidence, refuses nonempty condition lists and undecodable log lines (laundering must require consistent cross-bundle forgery, never a one-line edit — full erasure resistance inside bundle custody is impossible and is recorded as the honest boundary); (4) NEG-8 reference energies are re-reduced from primary evidence at the current mint at claim time (minutes-scale cost accepted), with canonical-workload identity (<code>canonical_neg8_workload</code> + <code>scientific_config_sha256</code> against the custody-bound config) enforced; (5) the four byte-frozen goldens carry executable sha256 pins. Round-4 confirmation follow-ups (same date): the universal <code>clock_anchor_unresolved</code> barrier covers the <code>0.4.1</code>/<code>0.4.2</code> arms (every pre-repair wire, not only 0.5.0/0.6.0 — the former 0.4.x escape is closed and its test assertion inverted); the production trace-margin gate uses the full three-term composed bound including the wall-minus-monotonic span; campaign <code>ready_for_analysis</code> requires a registered claim-eligible mint (<code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code>; mock telemetry exempt — it can never bear claims). Recorded custody boundary: the 24 h calibration horizon compares host wall time, so an operator with host time control can evade it — accepted (host time integrity is an operator obligation, like bundle custody itself).</li> </ol> <p>7b. <strong>(Fifth-wave addendum — calibration epistemics, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 5 over <code>09b5de6</code> (the P0 was statistical, not mechanical: a 40-pulse sample maximum is not an out-of-sample deterministic bound — 87.1% confidence on the 95th percentile vs the D-054 doctrine&#39;s n=59 for 95/95), the lead ruled: (1) <strong>protocol_v3</strong> raises the pulse count to 59, satisfying the repo&#39;s own nonparametric 95/95 doctrine; v3 is required for future claim-bearing calibration captures (v2 artifacts stay verifiable as this arc&#39;s validation evidence). (2) <strong>B_fiducial&#39;s epistemic status is stated honestly everywhere</strong>: a 95/95 nonparametric calibration bound, deterministic for claims only under REGISTERED transfer assumptions — T1 binding-vector stationarity, T2 the authenticated 24 h horizon, T3 load-regime transfer (calibration pulses are GPU-matmul under CPU-light load; sustained mixed-load transfer is an assumption; a loaded-calibration protocol variant is the registered roadmap mitigation). (3) <strong>Calibration bracketing is required for claim-bearing collections</strong>: two valid artifacts bracketing the window (pre at-or-before start, post at-or-after end, each within its own horizon), consumed as <code>max(pre, post)</code>, refusing <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code> or on bracket drift beyond <code>calibration_bracket_max_drift_s</code> (production 10 ms). Single-calibration reduction remains valid only for non-claim-bearing probe/exploratory use. (4) <strong>Environment state is window-enforced</strong>: per-interval thermal-pressure records are scanned over the measured window (<code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> refusal); admission objects are recomputed from their embedded snapshots — a stored <code>eligible: true</code> is never trusted. (5) <strong>Loop-termination doctrine</strong>: convergence sign-off means zero UNADDRESSED P0/P1, where &quot;addressed&quot; includes a registered limitation with recorded justification, adjudicated by the lead. A physical instrument&#39;s uncertainty budget always rests on stated assumptions; the honest end state is registered assumptions, not infinite hardening. T3 is the first entry in that register. Round-6 follow-up (same date): the bracket maximum must be CONSUMED, not merely recorded — a claim refuses <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code> whenever <code>max(B_pre, B_post)</code> exceeds any member envelope&#39;s minted effective bound (the member must be re-reduced under the dominating calibration); the whole-window producer refuses duplicated member occurrences (occurrence-count doctrine at the producer, not just the claim verifier); the registered-policy trust anchor refuses duplicate-JSON-key policy bytes; and the standalone reducer horizon predicate upper-bounds <code>run_started</code> as well as the window end. Round-7 follow-ups (same date): the operative floor is the EXACT maximum of the complete D-054 guarded floor over the joint per-member interval corners (every component is convex in the member vector, so vertex enumeration is exact; n &lt;= 16 enumerated, larger widths refuse) — the linear-corner residual widening alone under-covered the Student-t prediction component; claim-licensing whole-window evidence requires the registered policy to be production-profile AND claim-bearing (exploratory rows can never license claims); the bracket-dominance gate authenticates each member&#39;s consumed bound from hash-verified calibration evidence (never the mint-time metadata scalar, whose disagreement is itself provenance-invalid); claim brackets accept protocol v3 artifacts ONLY (v2 stays valid as reduction/validation evidence). Round-8 follow-ups (2026-07-22): calibration identity is SEMANTICALLY authenticated, not just byte-authenticated — every calibration command event&#39;s two clocks (top-level <code>timestamp_s</code> and embedded ClockStamp epoch) must agree within 1 s on the strict path, and any event carrying a ClockStamp is skew-checked (the live artifact agrees within 0.205 ms; a shifted-freshness relabel now refuses); claim-time rederivation authenticates the EXECUTED v3 schedule (pulse durations, the deterministic van-der-Corput gap sequence within ±0.25 s, ≥4.5 s commanded-quiet baselines) so phase-locked or degenerate captures cannot claim the 95/95 identity; and the canonical floor/MDE artifact carries the corner-widened floor additively (validator recomputes it; the analysis engine consumes the WIDENED guarded floor as operative) — closing the honest-artifact-fails-closed gap so a sound end-to-end floor/MDE handoff exists. Registry additions for this wave: <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code>, <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code>, (claim-bearing window not bracketed by two authenticated, fresh calibration artifacts, or bracket drift beyond the registered tolerance) and <code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> (per-interval thermal-pressure records non-nominal — or missing on the strict path — anywhere in the admission-to-window span). Both only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception for them is retired with this entry.</p> <ol start="7"> <li><p><strong>Sign-off evidence must be head-minted.</strong> Any artifact or re-reduction quoted as validation evidence for a head must be regenerated AT that head (the pre-233e9e3 rederived calibration artifact lacks the horizon fields the head requires, and the probe re-reductions predate the strict calibration gates — both are re-minted at the final head before the sign-off record is written). Claim-bearing measurement additionally requires fresh live [QUIET-MAC] calibration under protocol v3 (59 pulses, fifth-wave addendum), bracketing the window, within 24 h of collection.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Confirmation round 9 (2026-07-22, FINAL under the Ed-ratified cap) — outcome and registered limitation L1.</strong> The round-9 review over head 040ca3a confirmed the fiducial chain, reduce-side verification taxonomy, and contract coherence clean, with ONE surviving blocker (CR9-1, repro-backed, lead-reproduced): the canonical floor/MDE artifact is SELF-ATTESTING about its admissible half-widths and campaign membership — <code>validate_floor_artifact</code> recomputes widened floors only from artifact-internal widths, and evidence binding authenticates identities, hashes, and ordering but neither rederives source widths nor requires complete governed campaign membership. A substituted artifact with understated widths (or one omitting a member) validates, binds, and licenses an exact claim floor. Per the loop-termination doctrine (clause 5), the lead adjudicates this a REGISTERED LIMITATION rather than a tenth round:</p> <ul> <li><strong>L1 (registered): canonical floor artifacts are not independently claim-licensing.</strong> Until floor↔extraction binding lands, a claim-bearing analysis may consume a floor artifact ONLY when it was produced by the governed extraction in the same custody session as the analysis (same run manifest; extraction gates demonstrably executed). Standalone or externally supplied floor artifacts are non-claim-bearing evidence. Justification: the exposure is artifact substitution or a defective producer BETWEEN extraction and analysis; an honest same-session pipeline computes widths and membership under the already -hardened extraction gates, so no measurement this program will make under L1&#39;s workflow rule is affected. The gap is a third-party verifiability deficit, not an instrument-physics defect.</li> <li><strong>Queued fix (next cycle, P1):</strong> bind each canonical floor cell to its extraction report and source-member disposition (or rederive the extraction gates and widths at binding), refusing on any stored width/corner mismatch or membership deviation, with integration regressions for width substitution and member omission (TASK_QUEUE FLOOR-BIND-01). Round-9 verification note: the focused 357-test review surface passed at the head in-session; the lead&#39;s full-suite gate over the identical tree content (2088 passed / 15 skipped / 1570 subtests / 0 failures) stands as the aggregate confirmation.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>Live collection arc (2026-07-22/23) — collection-path regressions, occurrence supersession, and basis-scoped verdicts.</strong> The first live Window-A members after sign-off exposed collection-path defects invisible to nine review rounds without hardware; each was fixed under the ratified contracts (PR #80 canonical-attempt promotion + sole-sampler gapless design; PR #81 idle-slice cursor after forensics proved the slicer&#39;s own parsing contaminated the admission interval at the real ~120 ms powermetrics cadence). Two doctrine amendments were then ruled by the lead when the whole-window verdict path contradicted operational guidance (both defaults preserved, both overrides explicit and auditable):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Occurrence supersession (amends the round-6 occurrence-count doctrine):</strong> duplicated member occurrences still REFUSE by default; a duplicate may resolve to the present bundle only when an explicit operator supersession artifact (append-only, hash-sealed, naming the superseded occurrence, quarantine destination, and reason — <code>--record-supersession</code>) exists; two present bundles always refuse.</li> <li><strong>Basis-scoped whole-window verdicts:</strong> latest-wins remains rejected (verdict-shopping prevention); every verdict records a canonical evaluation-basis hash (member occurrence set + calibration bracket set<ul> <li>policy) and binds only that basis; consumers match the claim&#39;s basis; legacy basis-less verdict rows never govern new claims. Diagnostic-cascade decoupling and whole-window waiver consumption landed in the same wave. Windows a5 (108 members) and prior attempts remain NON-claim-bearing as whole windows (true clock-anchor refusal on one member; NEG-8 end reference measured ~2 h post-collection failed the drift gate at 0.778 J — the instrument correctly refusing a stale bracket); their corpora stand as instrument-proving evidence. The next clean bracketed window is the first claim attempt.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>NEG-8 drift-gate estimand ruling (2026-07-24; lead-ruled; RATIFIED in amended SCREEN+BUDGET form by the clause-10 addendum below — this original gross-only form was superseded the same day and never collected under).</strong> The whole-window drift adjudication proved the gate as previously implemented compared the two reference cells&#39; admissible envelopes at opposite corners (~0.9-1.5 J stacked) against an underived 0.05 J constant — structurally unpassable even for a physically perfect window (a8 measured point drift 0.006718 J over 2.96 h on ~38.5 J references). Ruling: the gate estimand is POINT DRIFT abs(end_point_gross − start_point_gross); the idle-subtracted point drift and the opposite-corner envelope statistic are recorded diagnostics, never gating (envelope stacking double-counts instrument uncertainty already composed into floor envelopes). The bound is DERIVED: a hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact minted by governed CLI from a named settled-reference corpus (n&gt;=10, predeclared estimator <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> = max(sample_range_j, t_{0.975,n-1}·s·sqrt(2))), consumed with full provenance in the verdict output. Registry addition: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (fail-closed refusal whenever no valid governed bound artifact exists). Windows a6/a8 may be re-verdicted under the derived bound (with explicit waivers for aborted-member fragments); a5 and a7 remain refused on their genuine grounds.</p> </li> </ol> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum — debate and Ed ratification (2026-07-24).</strong> Per Ed&#39;s direction the ruling was formally debated with the peer model before ratification. The peer DISAGREED with the ruling as written on one structural point and was adjudicated correct: the point-drift statistic is the right estimand but an anomaly screen is not proof of stability — passing the gate must never erase observed drift from the claim error budget (consistent with the repo&#39;s own D-054/D-057 language). Ed RATIFIED the amended SCREEN + BUDGET design (the debate&#39;s option F, full variant, Ed explicitly directing the maximal build): per-claim-family point-drift screens (gross AND idle-subtracted, each with its own derived bound); per-family drift ALLOWANCES propagated additively into every floor/claim envelope of the window, never zero even on passing windows (allowance = max(observed excursion, derived repeatability bound)); replicated endpoint references (n=3 per endpoint, means with standard errors) and one midpoint reference prospectively, with the allowance taken over the maximum absolute excursion across sampled points; drift-bound artifacts carry a freshness horizon and re-derivation triggers (OS/build, power-supply, calibration-identity changes) with a distinct stale-bound refusal spelling; legacy pair-only windows evaluate under the single-member-endpoint minimum. Ed&#39;s recorded guardrails: watch the RIGOR SPIRAL (floors inflating past the effect sizes the science needs — monitor floor-vs-expected-effect at every extraction) and NO INVENTED PHYSICS (no functional form without a defensible basis; stated limitations beat unjustified formulas). Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html:752:          <p class="deck">The 07-17 suite-cell inflation was root-caused to a macOS video screensaver engaging on an awake idle display — not the power source. An environment-guard admission system was built, adversarially reviewed through eight fix/audit rounds, merged, and then used to re-measure the suite cells in two bracketed quiet windows: <button class="datum" data-tip="Corpora: runs_recal_20260718 (32 bundles) + runs_recal2_20260719 (62 bundles); validate-bundle --strict, lead-run">94 strict-valid bundles</button>, every member satisfying all D-077 admission predicates (three baselines show CPU-side excursions the GPU-idle classifier does not gate — recorded, not hidden).</p>

<h1>JouleWise: Project Status, Plan, And Architecture</h1> <p>Audience: project advisor. This is the standalone monitoring document - it summarizes what the project is, how it is built, where it stands, and what it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository are provided for anyone who wants the full evidence trail.</p> <ul> <li>Freshness owner: phase completion lives in the phase exit checklists; live gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>; the canonical suite command and CI own the current verification result. This page deliberately does not duplicate volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.</li> <li>Repository state: <code>main</code> contains the repaired measurement instrument (D-078 phase 0) and the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10; council C-033). The repaired-instrument collection has 229 members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are useful diagnostic evidence that the instrument works, but they are not claim-bearing and do not yet publish a floor. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine collection following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>; if it passes, it will produce the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</li> <li>Project phase: see the phase exit checklists for exact completion state; live eligibility and next work come from the generated state kernel, not this reader-facing summary.</li> <li>Repository: <code>github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</code> (branch <code>main</code>)</li> <li>Live status site: <a href="https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app">https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app</a> (Lakebed capsule; it is an Ed-deployed snapshot, not the repository authority. <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code> records known differences; agents refresh that report when front-facing state changes and never regenerate or deploy the site.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="current-repository-view-30-second-read">Current Repository View — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The repaired instrument has completed its first collection era, but the first claim-grade floor is still ahead.</strong> The D-078 phase-0 repair fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22. Four bracketed windows then collected 229 strict members (a5-a8). They are retained as non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence: they showed that the repaired path works and exposed the remaining drift-screen problem, but they are not a published floor set.</p> <p>That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims. The next quiet session will mint its bound inside the window and collect three start references, one midpoint reference, and three end references. The older 222-bundle floor table below remains visible as a caveated historical record, not the current measurement posture.</p> <p>AXI-SB remains <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.</p> <h3>Published Window-A floor summary</h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>CAVEAT (2026-07-19 soundness audit):</strong> a trace-time-anchor defect was found in the powermetrics evidence path (power timestamps misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale). It affects the corpora behind this table; every row below is <strong>under re-adjudication</strong> and none should be cited as a promoted floor until the instrument is repaired and the rows re-extracted. Record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> </blockquote> <p>Every energy value below is a false-effect guard floor in joules on the <strong>Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary (CPU + GPU + ANE)</strong>. Gross is the D-067 headline basis; idle-subtracted values are labeled within-device secondary views. Absolute rows use repeated identical conditions; comparative rows use same-condition ABBA blocks. Each primary row uses <code>n=10</code> strict-valid bundles or ABBA blocks.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>window / basis</th> <th align="right">absolute floor</th> <th align="right">comparative floor</th> <th align="right">computed <code>floor_gate_j</code> / disposition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>mid request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.527 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mid request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.537 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.052 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.059 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>prefill phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.477 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>decode phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.786 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short-prefill stress, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.027 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">smoke-only; <code>not_resolvable_sample_count</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite item, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.333 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J; drift review required</td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite level, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.664 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J; drift review required</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>The start/end NEG-8 reference pair is an <code>n=2</code> drift diagnostic, not a campaign floor. Its gross request energy moved by 7.659 J; the idle-subtracted within-device secondary view moved by 6.608 J (same boundary). Verified extraction: <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json</code>; reader deliverable: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-17-window-a-brief.html</code>.</p> <h3>2026-07-19 re-calibration under the environment guard — PRELIMINARY</h3> <p>The caveated suite rows were re-measured in two bracketed windows under the D-077 guard: <strong>94 strict-valid bundles</strong>, all admission predicates satisfied. Reviewed readout: suite gross <strong>147.96 ± 0.39 J</strong> clean (contaminated cells were ~+30%); frozen-estimator provisional comparative floor <strong>≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%)</strong> from 5 of 10 planned ABBA blocks (~22× tighter, same estimator, than the caveated figure); long-decode <strong>83.9 mJ/output-token</strong>, matching the 07-17 decode cell to ~0.1%. That corpus was claim-ineligible on source provenance (dirty collection tree); details: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html</code>.</p> <p>UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid bundles with clean source provenance (<code>runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/</code>) cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n, including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source provenance gate is closed. <strong>SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.</strong> In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to ~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the workload&#39;s start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for sub-second test runs (one 0.37 s run read 0.27 J when its true consumption, plainly present in the recording, was <del>8 J), and a meaningful hidden uncertainty (</del>±10 J) even on 60-second runs. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply below this instrument&#39;s resolution and will not be claimed — by design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter&#39;s own timestamps, attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md</code>; technical record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and signed off.</strong> Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened relative to the model&#39;s work (the clock-alignment fix, with the alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with, mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is automatically rejected; and (c) refuses to report a result rather than report a doubtful one, in every failure case we could construct. One known limitation is recorded honestly: the file that stores the detection-floor statistics is not yet cryptographically tied back to the raw measurements it came from, so we only trust such files when our own pipeline produced them in the same verified session (a fix is queued). Live validation on the real hardware passed: the validation recording (made under the earlier 40-pulse calibration procedure) detected all 40 calibration pulses with no false detections, and a test measurement reproduced the expected physics where the old defective pipeline had been wrong by a factor of ~28. Production measurements will use the newer 59-pulse calibration procedure, which supports the stronger statistical guarantee we quote for the timing error bar. Next: a fresh calibration and re-collection of the measurement campaign under the repaired instrument. Record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-20-p0-instrument-repair.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>COLLECTION ERA UPDATE (2026-07-24): the repaired instrument has now been proven in production.</strong> Over two nights we collected 229 clean measurements across four properly-bracketed windows. The standout result: two identical reference measurements taken three hours apart agreed to within 0.007 joules on a ~38.5 joule task — about 0.02%, which is excellent repeatability for whole-system power measurement. The windows are not yet &quot;claim-grade&quot; for one honest reason: our own stability check (comparing a reference task at each window&#39;s start and end) was found to be asking a mathematically unanswerable question, so it failed every window on a technicality while the underlying data was good. After a formal debate between the two AI models working on the project — which the reviewing model won on one substantive point — the check was redesigned and ratified: windows are now screened for anomalous drift against a limit derived from measured repeatability (instead of an arbitrary constant), and any drift observed is carried into the results&#39; error bars rather than being ignored once a window &quot;passes&quot;. Reference measurements are also being tripled at each window edge. One collection session under the new rules produces the project&#39;s first claim-grade detection-floor table, which then sizes the Splitwise replication experiments. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-23-window-a-collection-arc.md</code>, decision log D-078 clauses 8-10.</p> <p><strong>SCREENING RULES BUILT, AUDITED, AND MERGED (2026-07-25; council C-033).</strong> The redesigned stability screen described above is now implemented and on main: both energy families are screened separately, every passing window carries an explicit drift allowance into its error bars, drift limits expire after 24 hours so stale calibrations cannot be reused, and a measurement whose internal clock had to be guessed can never anchor a result (that one rule alone corrected a floor that was overstated by roughly a factor of three). The code went through an unusually deep adversarial review — four independent audit rounds and three rounds of cross-examination between two different AI models — which caught and fixed several ways the new rules could have been silently bypassed. The step-by-step measurement procedure for the next collection session is written up in <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-24-screen-budget-gauntlet.md</code>, council log C-033.</p> <h3>Exploratory follow-on — not a promoted claim</h3> <p>Nine additional strict-valid, collection-usable bundles cover three repetitions each of unmatched OLMoE-1B-7B BF16, Qwen3-4B INT4, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4 configurations on the fixed five-item <code>jw_mixed_v1_sentinel</code> shape. Every bundle is claim-evidence-flagged, the model/config points differ in architecture, scale, tokenizer, and quantization, and the repetition count is below the headline protocol. The values are therefore descriptive <strong>EXPLORATORY / L1-legacy observations only</strong>.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J (227.141–231.790 J)</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token (177.454–181.086 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s (122.261–122.481 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J (362.642–362.903 J)</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token (283.314–283.518 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s (106.470–106.545 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J (1061.722–1085.144 J)</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token (829.471–847.769 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s (39.349–39.569 tok/s)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Each bundle emitted 1,280 generated output tokens. Gross per-output-token values above are derived from the gross suite numerator; the stored <code>energy_output_token_j</code> field instead uses the idle-subtracted numerator and is retained as a labeled within-device secondary view in the full extraction. For the like-for-like suite-level gross window on the Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary, the exploratory OLMoE-versus-Qwen3-4B mean gap is 133.720 J, above the published 24.619 J suite-level gross <code>floor_gate_j</code>. That only says the descriptive gap exceeds the measurement guard: unmatched configurations, evidence flags, drift review, and the lack of a prospective contrast still prohibit efficiency or architecture claims. Every aggregate and raw repetition is bundle-cited in <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-c-027-whole-project-council-review-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, C-027 whole-project council review) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The project put itself in front of a hostile examiner and corrected its own front page.</strong> A seven-lens cross-model review (new Codex model, extra-high reasoning) plus an independent final examiner audited the docs, the scientific claims, the statistics implementation, the architecture, and the operating loop itself. Verdict: the evidence discipline and instrument core are sound, but reader-facing claims had drifted from the evidence (the 1.5B per-token headline used the wrong denominator — now corrected as <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~79-90 mJ per generated output token), the D-053 contrast-CI machinery exists as binding specs but not yet as code (now owned as queue rows P2-037..P2-042 and gating Window-A interpretation), and the loop&#39;s own audit trail and the capstone-critical path (grading rubric, report skeleton, off-machine backup, one data-to-figure slice) need attention before any new breadth. All measured values above remain legacy L1 preliminary observations. Full adjudicated record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-09-c027-whole-project-review.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-advisor-status-cockpit-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, advisor status cockpit) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The public preview is being upgraded for live advisor observation.</strong> The project-status page remains generated from repository evidence, but Lakebed now has a narrow fail-soft live overlay contract: freshness from GitHub commit checks plus parsed current fields from <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>, <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>, and the risk register. The advisor cockpit adds live snapshot state, attention items, campaign readiness, evidence cards, and claim-ceiling panels; the Story page drops hand-authored volatile counts. The operational policy is D-051: repo markdown remains the source of truth and Lakebed never hides static provenance. Current work follows <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>: C-019 shakedown, then P2-015 quiet calibration for Window A (the CP-5 stop card was cleared 2026-07-09).</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-08-all-four-streams-merged-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-08, all four streams merged) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>Everything landed.</strong> The multi-stream session merged as four PRs: P2-013 and P2-014 are closed — all 31 audit pins fixed, the suite passed with zero expected failures (current count authority is RUN_STATE.md Current Verification; the suite-build merge was 732 tests and the post-alignment state is 734), bundle provenance now records prompt/workload identities, and <code>validate-bundle --strict</code> includes the powermetrics raw-plist-to-trace gate plus the legacy additive-summary comparison. The six existing real corpus bundles pass strict read-only and unrewritten; strict proves re-derivation of the recorded evidence, not independent rerunning of the hardware session. New-era bundles must carry shape-valid provenance to pass. The Stage 3.0.1 KV spike is merged with a lead-reverified verdict of <code>replay_supported</code> (tokens identical; cache size +0.018% vs prediction) — Phase 3&#39;s central technical risk is retired on current hardware. The fixture-first 2K NVIDIA stack is merged; ALL its protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until first live hardware contact (the live-verification checklist is ready). The independent project critique now carries a second-pass reassessment (its recommendations that became code are marked resolved; 16/17 of its checkable claims were lead-verified against file evidence): <code>docs/project_critique_review.html</code>. Next: the detection-floor calibration (P2-015) then the 2M two-model baseline campaign on a quiet machine. Reader-facing status below defers to the phase checklist matrix rows for per-item authority.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fifth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fifth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The instrument grew four capabilities in one session and is now campaign-ready.</strong> <em>(Historical claim; C-027 (2026-07-09) supersedes the gating: execution is conditioned on P0-003 backup, P2-038, P2-039, and P2-015-SMOKE.)</em> Five parallel work streams landed (PRs #2-#6): (1) <strong>statistical uncertainty</strong> — every multi-repetition experiment now carries per-metric 95% confidence intervals with outlier detection and explicit below-protocol flags, re-derivable byte-identically from the raw evidence bundles (verified on a live 3-repetition run as <strong>D-014 verification workload, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> 99.19 ± 1.36 mJ/output-token); (2) <strong>contamination detection</strong> — an idle-window quality gate that mechanically flags runs taken on a non-quiet machine (it caught its first real contamination during verification); (3) <strong>deep telemetry</strong> — per-sample GPU/CPU-cluster frequency and residency forensics plus a machine-state snapshot in every bundle; (4) <strong>campaign automation</strong> — a deterministic config-matrix generator and a resumable sequential runner, so the planned two-model baseline matrix (4 workload shapes × 2 models × 5 repetitions) runs unattended. A review council also produced a hardware-tiered research agenda: 16 questions answerable on current hardware alone, 10 more behind planned gates (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The P2-013 evidence-integrity and P2-014 provenance fixes are now complete; next Mac corpus step is the baseline matrix on a quiet machine.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fourth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fourth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>A flagship-class model is now benchmarked.</strong> Qwen3.5-122B (Feb 2026 generation, 122B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 10B active, a reasoning model) ran through the identical harness and workload on the M3 Max. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. Throughput was 46 tokens/s, and the gross-energy sample CV was 0.3% across three sequential repetitions in one warm-cache session. The earlier model recorded <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per request and <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~87 mJ per generated output token at 257 tok/s. <em>(Metric bases and CV wording corrected 2026-07-09, C-027.)</em> First cross-model finding: the two measured points differ in size, architecture, and quantization, so they are not a demonstrated scaling law. They are, however, consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal structure Q4 models: <strong>unsubtracted decode-window mean power — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~23.5 W for P2-003 and ~27.5 W for FLAGSHIP-001, while the bigger model&#39;s cost showed up mostly as time. Also this update: the research agenda grew to six named questions (Q4-Q6) after a multi-model review council, with a curated question bank (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>) and an instrument roadmap (richer telemetry parsing, a difficulty-graded scored workload suite, and implementing the statistical-uncertainty protocol) queued.</p> <h2 id="update-ledger">Update Ledger</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>date</th> <th>label</th> <th>one-line outcome</th> <th>run-report link</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Measurement-soundness audit (Ed-directed)</td> <td>VERDICT: unsound for claim-bearing use as recorded — trace-time-anchor defect misattributes request/phase energies (all four P0s lead-verified); metric-level prechecks already failed 238/288 request metrics; four cooldown cap hits unjoined; analysis-engine wire incompat. lead gate pending)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-17</td> <td>Window A floors + advisor brief</td> <td>PRs #72/#74 closed the bounded powermetrics drain defects and P2-038 passed on merged main; PR #73 filed the AXI-SC negative verdict; Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; idle-subtracted is a labeled within-device secondary view</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-068</td> <td>Site deployment is Ed-manual; sessions end with a drift report, never a deploy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-069</td> <td>Advisor-doc alignment (stream S-0) is sanctioned front-facing work</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-070</td> <td>Architectural-axes extension agenda (AXI): scope, claim posture, batch-axis rulings</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-071</td> <td>G10 memory-fit rule ratified (axi-sd-memory-fit-shape-v1); device-list review opened</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-072</td> <td>Standing self-merge-with-full-gate authority (gh merges included)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-073">D-073</a></td> <td>D-016 device-list amendment: Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-074">D-074</a></td> <td>Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-075">D-075</a></td> <td>Extension-axis intake: ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-076">D-076</a></td> <td>Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review): measured-first budgets</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-077">D-077</a></td> <td>Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log.html#d-078">D-078</a></td> <td>Soundness gate: no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</td> <td>accepted; operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
