class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Anything user-facing (push/merge/publish) follows the user&#39;s standing instructions.</p> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Date</th> <th>Topic</th> <th>Outcome</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>C-001</td> <td>2026-07-06</td> <td>Adopt review/counterreview between Claude and Codex (2H precedent)</td> <td>adopted; Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. id="d-078-soundness-gate-no-claim-bearing-extraction-from-time-anchor-defective-powermetrics-corpora">D-078: Soundness gate — no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-19. Owner: lead session under Ed&#39;s soundness-audit directive; recorded so the gate binds future sessions immediately. Status update 2026-07-22: the gate has been operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the entire repair arc, and Ed explicitly ratified the close-out cap (clause 8); formal ratification of this original text rides the PR #79 review (Ed may amend).</p> <p>The 2026-07-19 measurement-soundness audit (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>; all P0 findings lead-verified from primary evidence) found that powermetrics trace timestamps are misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale (pre-spawn/first-parse midpoint anchor), making request/phase/item point energies physically non-attributable as recorded across ALL existing powermetrics corpora, including the 2026-07-17 published floor extraction.</p> <p>Binding until amended:</p> <ol> <li>No claim-bearing floor, MDE, or L2/L3 energy claim may be published from any corpus collected under the defective anchor. Existing corpora are instrument/calibration evidence only.</li> <li>Extraction must treat <code>window_evidence_precheck</code> as a hard gate and must join campaign-log cooldown/admission evidence (cap hits are not clean n). &quot;Claim-eligible&quot; narrative language may describe METRIC-level eligibility only, never source provenance alone.</li> <li>The repair path (roadmap Phase 0, <code>docs/phase_2/splitwise_replication_roadmap.md</code>): tight causal anchor + anchor-shift joule envelope in reduction, analysis-engine 0.5.0/v2 wire compat, CPU-aware idle admission, prospective NEG-8 acceptance threshold. Stored summaries are never rewritten; fixes are prospective.</li> <li>The 2026-07-17 published floor table is caveated in PROJECT_STATUS pending re-extraction; advisor-brief/site correction timing is Ed&#39;s deployment decision (D-068).</li> </ol> <p>Revisit trigger: Phase 0 repair lands with live pulse-validation evidence, or Ed rules a different salvage/disposition for existing corpora.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-20: fail-closed vocabulary and immutable summaries</h3> <p>Additive amendment under the adversarial soundness fix round. The following spellings are the binding, closed registry for D-078 claim refusals and campaign conditions. and <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li>Floor-extraction refusals: <code>bundle_missing</code>, <code>summary_unreadable</code>, <code>bundle_strict_invalid</code>, <code>whole_window_neg8_verdict_missing</code>, <code>whole_window_neg8_verdict_failed</code>, <code>adapter_continuity_evidence_missing</code>, <code>adapter_continuity_failed</code>, <code>cpu_admission_core_missing</code>, and <code>cpu_admission_core_failed</code>.</li> <li>Idle-admission/campaign conditions: <code>cpu_baseline_telemetry_missing</code>, <code>cpu_baseline_telemetry_malformed</code>, <code>cpu_baseline_sample_count_insufficient</code>, <code>cpu_busy_ratio_p95_exceeded</code>, <code>processor_combined_power_w_p95_exceeded</code>, Stored summary bytes are now immutable evidence. Post-hoc reduction writes a new, non-clobbering artifact (including the repaired anchor envelope) or refuses; the raw-artifact immutability and pure-reducer portions of D-002/D-028 remain in force. Frozen 0.5.0/0.6.0 numeric semantics remain replayable and are not claim-bearing merely because they can be read.</p> <h3>D-078 additive registry addendum — 2026-07-20: causal-set repair</h3> <p>The closed registry additionally includes floor/whole-window barriers <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_coverage_incomplete</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code>, and <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. These additions only refuse or widen uncertainty; none can license a claim.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21: convergence fix wave (lead adjudications)</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the two-round cross-model convergence loop over <code>impl/p0-instrument-repair</code> (round-2 and round-3 fix waves; council log carries the layer accounting). Six rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Additive causal-bound composition.</strong> <code>B_effective = B_bundle + B_fiducial</code> replaces <code>max(B_bundle, B_fiducial)</code>. The bundle-local censored-constraint anchor interval and the instrument&#39;s emission-lag bound sit on disjoint causal links; no containment proof exists, so <code>max()</code> under-composes. <code>B_fiducial</code> itself additively folds in the calibration capture&#39;s own trace-anchor bound. The prior <code>max()</code> text in this log is superseded prospectively; stored summaries are never rewritten.</li> <li><strong>Identity bump, not in-place semantics change.</strong> The additive composition, fiducial protocol_v2 physics (<code>joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2</code> full 2-D branch-and-bound region), and the stricter evidence-admission semantics are minted as reducer <code>0.5.2</code> / AXI <code>0.6.2</code> with <code>configs/calibration/powermetrics_fiducial/protocol_v2.json</code>. <code>0.5.1</code> / <code>0.6.1</code> and <code>protocol_v1.json</code> remain byte-frozen replay arms.</li> <li><strong>Superseded arms are claim-ineligible.</strong> <code>0.5.1</code>/<code>0.6.1</code> summaries refuse claim-bearing use with a registered refusal (superseded max-composition envelope semantics); <code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code> are the sole claim-eligible mints.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions (closing the F11/PENDING exception).</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>token_count_stream_chunk_fallback</code> (renamed from the source-label reuse of <code>stream_chunk_fallback</code>), <code>pulse_calibration_rollover_gate_timeout</code> (pre-workload rollover gate timeout now refuses fail-closed, no artifact minting), and <code>post_window_trace_tail_shorter_than_anchor_bound</code> (reduce-time refusal when the post-window trace tail cannot support the composed anchor bound; collection policy raises the minimum post-window dwell to 1.0 s). These only refuse; none can license a claim.</li> <li><strong>Registry closure is one-way by design.</strong> Every emitted spelling must be registered here; a registered spelling with no current emission site (e.g. <code>window_evidence_precheck_failed</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>) is permitted — unemittable names cannot launder anything.</li> <li><strong>Member-level <code>claim_evidence_flags</code> is an all-leaf union — documented, not changed.</strong> Adjudicated a documentation defect only: the union is fail-safe (it can only over-flag, never over-admit) and gating decisions read the per-metric leaves. Scope documented in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>; no wire rename.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (second): two-edge envelope and confirmation-round rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the first confirmation round over <code>5093355</code> correctly withheld sign-off (fresh Sol xhigh audit; 8 confirmed findings, one P0). Rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Corner-composed two-edge envelope (P0 repair).</strong> The calibration fits independent start-edge and stop-edge emission lags; a single common trace shift under-covers because independent endpoint errors move energy by up to <code>2·P·B_fiducial</code> even when a common shift cancels. The claim envelope is now the extrema over start = <code>delta_common + eps_on</code>, stop = <code>delta_common + eps_off</code> with <code>|delta_common| &lt;= B_bundle</code> and <code>|eps_on|, |eps_off| &lt;= B_fiducial</code> independent. For nonnegative power the energy is monotone in each edge separately, so exact extrema are attained at the four edge corners with the common shift scanned continuously — the existing breakpoint-exact scan run per corner. The per-edge corner offset is <code>±(B_fiducial + wall_minus_monotonic_span)</code>: the span is a third disjoint per-edge error source, folded into the corners (delta-review amendment) rather than the frozen arms&#39; cruder <code>2·span·maxP</code> additive term, and the composed <code>anchor_bound_s</code> = <code>B_bundle + B_fiducial + span</code> governs the tail-sufficiency gate identically. Idle-subtracted and per-token envelopes additionally widen by <code>2·(B_fiducial + span)·P_idle</code> because independent edges vary the subtracted idle duration (delta re-audit catch). New registered method spelling for the 0.5.2/0.6.2 mints; v1/v2 spellings remain replay-read-only.</li> <li><strong>In-place revision of the unreleased mints.</strong> Reducer 0.5.2 / AXI 0.6.2 were never merged or used for stored artifacts; their envelope semantics are revised in place (no 0.5.3/0.6.3 inflation). Goldens regenerated and hand-verified against the formula.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions.</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>negative_power_sample</code> (negative rail power reaching the envelope/energy path breaks the monotonicity argument and refuses fail-closed) and <code>instrument_calibration_stale</code> (calibration artifacts now record capture wall time and a 24 h <code>max_age_s</code> validity horizon in protocol_v2; claim-time verification refuses missing/invalid capture time or age exceeded — a finite 40-pulse residual maximum is not an out-of-sample bound without recency enforcement). Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>capture_time_missing_or_invalid</code> (a v2 capture without a valid recorded capture wall time is invalid at minting, with the reason stated rather than silent). All only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception is retired with this entry. Replay purity note: the 0.5.1/0.6.1 arms keep their frozen binding expectation against the protocol_v2.json bytes current at their mint (<code>REPLAY_PROTOCOL_V2_SHA256</code>); custody-manifest verification and the staleness horizon are current-mint gates only.</li> <li><strong>Environment admission consumes the full evidence object.</strong> The shared validator fails closed on <code>critical_environment_passed</code>, <code>reference_provenance_present</code>, per-run evaluation eligibility, guard observations, and schema identity — and the post-run environment observation passes through the failure predicate on claim/whole-window paths (a post-run critical-environment failure refuses claim eligibility). This closes the Window-A screensaver contamination class end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>Calibration custody verified at claim time.</strong> The reducer enforces the validation-manifest reference: in-bundle containment, manifest hash, and presence + sha256 of every manifest member; any failure refuses as <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>. Current-era (0.5.2/0.6.2) claim-bearing use requires a protocol_v2 calibration artifact.</li> <li><strong>Collection floors.</strong> The 1.0 s post-window dwell minimum is enforced on every collection path (controller default, schema minimum, campaign-policy validation); sub-minimum configs refuse at validation. Scope spelling (delta-review adjudication): controller/CLI pre-collection rejection applies wherever powermetrics telemetry collects; mock-backend runs are not dwell-gated at the controller (mock telemetry cannot reach any claim path), while the campaign-policy schema minimum applies universally. Inner phase/item/block/level window entries carry the whole-trace anchor/calibration/tail barrier stamps whenever the top-level barrier fires.</li> <li><strong>Cooldown terminal-evidence normativity documented.</strong> The required terminal JSONL row fields (<code>release</code>, <code>release_criteria_met_late</code>), the cap-first precedence rule (&quot;the cap is causal and wins&quot;), and rejection semantics are contract text in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>, matching <code>joulewise/cooldown.py</code> exactly.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (third): provenance authentication rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after confirmation round 2 over <code>233e9e3</code> withheld sign-off (9 confirmed; the physics verified clean from every lens — all findings are provenance/governance). Rulings, implemented in the round-3 fix wave (frozen 0.5.1/0.6.1 replay semantics unchanged throughout):</p> <ol> <li><strong>Declared facts are authenticated against primary bytes.</strong> The calibration&#39;s declared <code>capture_wall_time_s</code> must agree (±1 s) with the capture time independently derived from the hash-verified source events — a stale calibration can no longer be relabeled fresh (the P0).</li> <li><strong>Freshness covers the whole measurement.</strong> The 24 h horizon binds both <code>run_started</code> and the measured window END: <code>capture &lt;= run_started</code> and <code>window_end &lt;= capture + max_age_s</code>, inclusive. Pre-run delays cannot carry sampling past the declared validity of its calibration.</li> <li><strong>Version identity is validated generically.</strong> Generic bundle validation checks <code>reducer_version</code> against the closed known set and the §8.1 version/event-semantics pairing rules as a validation-time structured problem (no wire-schema enum — frozen-arm byte replay preserved); an unsupported <code>--reducer-version</code> yields the standard structured refusal, never a traceback.</li> <li><strong>Stored verdicts are re-derived, never trusted.</strong> The whole-window verifier rejects duplicated NEG-8 core members (occurrence-count semantics) and re-derives the bracket verdict from member evidence; disagreement with the stored row is <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Delta-review strengthening (lead ruling): the re-derivation tolerances come from the repo-REGISTERED campaign policy whose file hash matches the row&#39;s <code>policy_sha256</code> — the one trust anchor that does not terminate at bundle custody. Unknown policy hashes, and rows whose self-asserted tolerances disagree with the registered policy, refuse <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> before re-derivation. The custody boundary is otherwise explicit: a forger with bundle write access can rewrite row-internal hashes consistently, but cannot mint a matching tracked policy file.</li> <li><strong>Protocol identity is shape-authenticated.</strong> A v2 <code>protocol_id</code> requires the v2 estimator identity, capture/horizon fields, and v2 residual shape; v1-shaped bodies relabeled v2 refuse <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li><strong>Admission attempts have timing semantics.</strong> Attempt-ledger rows carry strictly increasing, non-overlapping declared windows on the strict path; violations refuse <code>environment_admission_missing</code>. 7a. <strong>(Fourth-wave addendum — claim-aggregation rulings, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 3 over <code>0925480</code> (instrument core verified defensible on fresh head collections by every lens; all four P0s in the claim-aggregation layer), the lead ruled: (1) floors/MDEs widen by EXACT linear-corner evaluation over member envelope intervals — residual widening <code>w_i·(n−1)/n + Σ_{j≠i}w_j/n</code>, contrast widening <code>Σ|c_i|·w_i</code> — never a max-width shortcut, and the dominance refusal fires against the widened quantity; (2) admission is causally bound to its run: the final attempt window ends at-or-before window start within <code>MAX_ADMISSION_GAP_S = 600</code> (inclusive), the post-run observation is captured at-or-after window end, and attempt windows must contain their stage&#39;s recorded idle-capture interval; (3) the whole-window verifier re-derives CPU admission and adapter continuity from member-bundle primary evidence, refuses nonempty condition lists and undecodable log lines (laundering must require consistent cross-bundle forgery, never a one-line edit — full erasure resistance inside bundle custody is impossible and is recorded as the honest boundary); (4) NEG-8 reference energies are re-reduced from primary evidence at the current mint at claim time (minutes-scale cost accepted), with canonical-workload identity (<code>canonical_neg8_workload</code> + <code>scientific_config_sha256</code> against the custody-bound config) enforced; (5) the four byte-frozen goldens carry executable sha256 pins. Round-4 confirmation follow-ups (same date): the universal <code>clock_anchor_unresolved</code> barrier covers the <code>0.4.1</code>/<code>0.4.2</code> arms (every pre-repair wire, not only 0.5.0/0.6.0 — the former 0.4.x escape is closed and its test assertion inverted); the production trace-margin gate uses the full three-term composed bound including the wall-minus-monotonic span; campaign <code>ready_for_analysis</code> requires a registered claim-eligible mint (<code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code>; mock telemetry exempt — it can never bear claims). Recorded custody boundary: the 24 h calibration horizon compares host wall time, so an operator with host time control can evade it — accepted (host time integrity is an operator obligation, like bundle custody itself).</li> </ol> <p>7b. <strong>(Fifth-wave addendum — calibration epistemics, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 5 over <code>09b5de6</code> (the P0 was statistical, not mechanical: a 40-pulse sample maximum is not an out-of-sample deterministic bound — 87.1% confidence on the 95th percentile vs the D-054 doctrine&#39;s n=59 for 95/95), the lead ruled: (1) <strong>protocol_v3</strong> raises the pulse count to 59, satisfying the repo&#39;s own nonparametric 95/95 doctrine; v3 is required for future claim-bearing calibration captures (v2 artifacts stay verifiable as this arc&#39;s validation evidence). (2) <strong>B_fiducial&#39;s epistemic status is stated honestly everywhere</strong>: a 95/95 nonparametric calibration bound, deterministic for claims only under REGISTERED transfer assumptions — T1 binding-vector stationarity, T2 the authenticated 24 h horizon, T3 load-regime transfer (calibration pulses are GPU-matmul under CPU-light load; sustained mixed-load transfer is an assumption; a loaded-calibration protocol variant is the registered roadmap mitigation). (3) <strong>Calibration bracketing is required for claim-bearing collections</strong>: two valid artifacts bracketing the window (pre at-or-before start, post at-or-after end, each within its own horizon), consumed as <code>max(pre, post)</code>, refusing <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code> or on bracket drift beyond <code>calibration_bracket_max_drift_s</code> (production 10 ms). Single-calibration reduction remains valid only for non-claim-bearing probe/exploratory use. (4) <strong>Environment state is window-enforced</strong>: per-interval thermal-pressure records are scanned over the measured window (<code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> refusal); admission objects are recomputed from their embedded snapshots — a stored <code>eligible: true</code> is never trusted. (5) <strong>Loop-termination doctrine</strong>: convergence sign-off means zero UNADDRESSED P0/P1, where &quot;addressed&quot; includes a registered limitation with recorded justification, adjudicated by the lead. A physical instrument&#39;s uncertainty budget always rests on stated assumptions; the honest end state is registered assumptions, not infinite hardening. T3 is the first entry in that register. Round-6 follow-up (same date): the bracket maximum must be CONSUMED, not merely recorded — a claim refuses <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code> whenever <code>max(B_pre, B_post)</code> exceeds any member envelope&#39;s minted effective bound (the member must be re-reduced under the dominating calibration); the whole-window producer refuses duplicated member occurrences (occurrence-count doctrine at the producer, not just the claim verifier); the registered-policy trust anchor refuses duplicate-JSON-key policy bytes; and the standalone reducer horizon predicate upper-bounds <code>run_started</code> as well as the window end. Round-7 follow-ups (same date): the operative floor is the EXACT maximum of the complete D-054 guarded floor over the joint per-member interval corners (every component is convex in the member vector, so vertex enumeration is exact; n &lt;= 16 enumerated, larger widths refuse) — the linear-corner residual widening alone under-covered the Student-t prediction component; claim-licensing whole-window evidence requires the registered policy to be production-profile AND claim-bearing (exploratory rows can never license claims); the bracket-dominance gate authenticates each member&#39;s consumed bound from hash-verified calibration evidence (never the mint-time metadata scalar, whose disagreement is itself provenance-invalid); claim brackets accept protocol v3 artifacts ONLY (v2 stays valid as reduction/validation evidence). Round-8 follow-ups (2026-07-22): calibration identity is SEMANTICALLY authenticated, not just byte-authenticated — every calibration command event&#39;s two clocks (top-level <code>timestamp_s</code> and embedded ClockStamp epoch) must agree within 1 s on the strict path, and any event carrying a ClockStamp is skew-checked (the live artifact agrees within 0.205 ms; a shifted-freshness relabel now refuses); claim-time rederivation authenticates the EXECUTED v3 schedule (pulse durations, the deterministic van-der-Corput gap sequence within ±0.25 s, ≥4.5 s commanded-quiet baselines) so phase-locked or degenerate captures cannot claim the 95/95 identity; and the canonical floor/MDE artifact carries the corner-widened floor additively (validator recomputes it; the analysis engine consumes the WIDENED guarded floor as operative) — closing the honest-artifact-fails-closed gap so a sound end-to-end floor/MDE handoff exists. Registry additions for this wave: <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code>, <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code>, (claim-bearing window not bracketed by two authenticated, fresh calibration artifacts, or bracket drift beyond the registered tolerance) and <code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> (per-interval thermal-pressure records non-nominal — or missing on the strict path — anywhere in the admission-to-window span). Both only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception for them is retired with this entry.</p> <ol start="7"> <li><p><strong>Sign-off evidence must be head-minted.</strong> Any artifact or re-reduction quoted as validation evidence for a head must be regenerated AT that head (the pre-233e9e3 rederived calibration artifact lacks the horizon fields the head requires, and the probe re-reductions predate the strict calibration gates — both are re-minted at the final head before the sign-off record is written). Claim-bearing measurement additionally requires fresh live [QUIET-MAC] calibration under protocol v3 (59 pulses, fifth-wave addendum), bracketing the window, within 24 h of collection.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Confirmation round 9 (2026-07-22, FINAL under the Ed-ratified cap) — outcome and registered limitation L1.</strong> The round-9 review over head 040ca3a confirmed the fiducial chain, reduce-side verification taxonomy, and contract coherence clean, with ONE surviving blocker (CR9-1, repro-backed, lead-reproduced): the canonical floor/MDE artifact is SELF-ATTESTING about its admissible half-widths and campaign membership — <code>validate_floor_artifact</code> recomputes widened floors only from artifact-internal widths, and evidence binding authenticates identities, hashes, and ordering but neither rederives source widths nor requires complete governed campaign membership. A substituted artifact with understated widths (or one omitting a member) validates, binds, and licenses an exact claim floor. Per the loop-termination doctrine (clause 5), the lead adjudicates this a REGISTERED LIMITATION rather than a tenth round:</p> <ul> <li><strong>L1 (registered): canonical floor artifacts are not independently claim-licensing.</strong> Until floor↔extraction binding lands, a claim-bearing analysis may consume a floor artifact ONLY when it was produced by the governed extraction in the same custody session as the analysis (same run manifest; extraction gates demonstrably executed). Standalone or externally supplied floor artifacts are non-claim-bearing evidence. Justification: the exposure is artifact substitution or a defective producer BETWEEN extraction and analysis; an honest same-session pipeline computes widths and membership under the already -hardened extraction gates, so no measurement this program will make under L1&#39;s workflow rule is affected. The gap is a third-party verifiability deficit, not an instrument-physics defect.</li> <li><strong>Queued fix (next cycle, P1):</strong> bind each canonical floor cell to its extraction report and source-member disposition (or rederive the extraction gates and widths at binding), refusing on any stored width/corner mismatch or membership deviation, with integration regressions for width substitution and member omission (TASK_QUEUE FLOOR-BIND-01). Round-9 verification note: the focused 357-test review surface passed at the head in-session; the lead&#39;s full-suite gate over the identical tree content (2088 passed / 15 skipped / 1570 subtests / 0 failures) stands as the aggregate confirmation.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>Live collection arc (2026-07-22/23) — collection-path regressions, occurrence supersession, and basis-scoped verdicts.</strong> The first live Window-A members after sign-off exposed collection-path defects invisible to nine review rounds without hardware; each was fixed under the ratified contracts (PR #80 canonical-attempt promotion + sole-sampler gapless design; PR #81 idle-slice cursor after forensics proved the slicer&#39;s own parsing contaminated the admission interval at the real ~120 ms powermetrics cadence). Two doctrine amendments were then ruled by the lead when the whole-window verdict path contradicted operational guidance (both defaults preserved, both overrides explicit and auditable):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Occurrence supersession (amends the round-6 occurrence-count doctrine):</strong> duplicated member occurrences still REFUSE by default; a duplicate may resolve to the present bundle only when an explicit operator supersession artifact (append-only, hash-sealed, naming the superseded occurrence, quarantine destination, and reason — <code>--record-supersession</code>) exists; two present bundles always refuse.</li> <li><strong>Basis-scoped whole-window verdicts:</strong> latest-wins remains rejected (verdict-shopping prevention); every verdict records a canonical evaluation-basis hash (member occurrence set + calibration bracket set<ul> <li>policy) and binds only that basis; consumers match the claim&#39;s basis; legacy basis-less verdict rows never govern new claims. Diagnostic-cascade decoupling and whole-window waiver consumption landed in the same wave. Windows a5 (108 members) and prior attempts remain NON-claim-bearing as whole windows (true clock-anchor refusal on one member; NEG-8 end reference measured ~2 h post-collection failed the drift gate at 0.778 J — the instrument correctly refusing a stale bracket); their corpora stand as instrument-proving evidence. The next clean bracketed window is the first claim attempt.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>NEG-8 drift-gate estimand ruling (2026-07-24; lead-ruled; RATIFIED in amended SCREEN+BUDGET form by the clause-10 addendum below — this original gross-only form was superseded the same day and never collected under).</strong> The whole-window drift adjudication proved the gate as previously implemented compared the two reference cells&#39; admissible envelopes at opposite corners (~0.9-1.5 J stacked) against an underived 0.05 J constant — structurally unpassable even for a physically perfect window (a8 measured point drift 0.006718 J over 2.96 h on ~38.5 J references). Ruling: the gate estimand is POINT DRIFT abs(end_point_gross − start_point_gross); the idle-subtracted point drift and the opposite-corner envelope statistic are recorded diagnostics, never gating (envelope stacking double-counts instrument uncertainty already composed into floor envelopes). The bound is DERIVED: a hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact minted by governed CLI from a named settled-reference corpus (n&gt;=10, predeclared estimator <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> = max(sample_range_j, t_{0.975,n-1}·s·sqrt(2))), consumed with full provenance in the verdict output. Registry addition: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (fail-closed refusal whenever no valid governed bound artifact exists). Windows a6/a8 may be re-verdicted under the derived bound (with explicit waivers for aborted-member fragments); a5 and a7 remain refused on their genuine grounds.</p> </li> </ol> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum — debate and Ed ratification (2026-07-24).</strong> Per Ed&#39;s direction the ruling was formally debated with the peer model before ratification. The peer DISAGREED with the ruling as written on one structural point and was adjudicated correct: the point-drift statistic is the right estimand but an anomaly screen is not proof of stability — passing the gate must never erase observed drift from the claim error budget (consistent with the repo&#39;s own D-054/D-057 language). Ed RATIFIED the amended SCREEN + BUDGET design (the debate&#39;s option F, full variant, Ed explicitly directing the maximal build): per-claim-family point-drift screens (gross AND idle-subtracted, each with its own derived bound); per-family drift ALLOWANCES propagated additively into every floor/claim envelope of the window, never zero even on passing windows (allowance = max(observed excursion, derived repeatability bound)); replicated endpoint references (n=3 per endpoint, means with standard errors) and one midpoint reference prospectively, with the allowance taken over the maximum absolute excursion across sampled points; drift-bound artifacts carry a freshness horizon and re-derivation triggers (OS/build, power-supply, calibration-identity changes) with a distinct stale-bound refusal spelling; legacy pair-only windows evaluate under the single-member-endpoint minimum. Ed&#39;s recorded guardrails: watch the RIGOR SPIRAL (floors inflating past the effect sizes the science needs — monitor floor-vs-expected-effect at every extraction) and NO INVENTED PHYSICS (no functional form without a defensible basis; stated limitations beat unjustified formulas). Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. scope enforcement caught the lead&#39;s own stray file (adjudicated benign); floors: request 0.527/0.052 J, phase 1.477/0.786 J, ABBA comparative w/ flagged tail drift; exploratory gross suite: OLMoE ~229 J vs Qwen3-4B ~362.8 J vs 122B ~1072 J (exploratory-labeled) | | C-036 | 2026-07-16 | Resumption + no-hardware batch (Ed: audits in a workflow + &quot;handle the merge yourself if all is well... get the project ready for my quiet mac&quot;; full record <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-16-resumption-nohw-batch.md</code>, the ONE home): ultracode readiness workflow (4 Sol-high audits + severity-tiered refuters) BEFORE work selection; then 4 streams (SPLIT-AP xhigh contract tier, SITE-02 high standard, AXI-SB xhigh spike, AXI-SD Fable web-verification); every fix round delta-re-audited; three self-merges under Ed&#39;s in-session delegation, each with the full D-031-amended gate | PRs #67 (<code>7593259</code>, AXI-SA + CI portability fix after the audit caught red CI), #68 (<code>2778ed2</code>, SITE-02 — D2 step verified EXECUTED in the CI log), #69 (<code>9db4546</code>, SPLIT-AP freeze) merged; delta re-audit caught a LEAD-pinned predictor defect (8th fix-rounds-inject-defects datum, first lead-authored); AXI-SD memo: OLMo pair d_active 0.0016 + 8GB-fit may moot Option A&#39;s premise, Qwen3 pair confirmed-fails G10 (17.17 GB) |</p> <hr> <h2 id="full-entry">Full entry</h2> <h2>C-028: C-027 adjudication and integration arc — infrastructure wave, PRs #49/#54/#55, and the integration window (2026-07-10/11)</h2> <p>Full record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code>; binding rulings: <code>docs/specs/c027/ADJUDICATION.md</code>. No tracked <code>docs/process_traces/</code> artifact is present in this checkout; the run report&#39;s aggregate invocation record is therefore the durable evidence available for this arc, and D-064 governs future tracked event streams. This limitation is recorded rather than repaired with an invented pointer. The arc&#39;s earlier segment (adjudication rounds, PRs #41–#48) is recorded in the CP-5/checkpoint records and stop-card history; this entry records the 2026-07-10/11 continuation.</p> <p>Participants: Fable lead; gpt-5.6-sol as implementer, reviewer, refuter, auditor, and design consultant across ~57 recorded invocations. The lead retained worktree/merge authority, every final diff gate, all live verification, and bookkeeping.</p> <p>Scope of this segment: PR #49 (NV-GATE-2 code-now + flake root-causes) merged <code>1b0f1f6</code> + <code>10e0ad2</code>; PR #54 (P2-041 vetted rebuild from the RED-tranche triage recipe, review + fix round + delta review) merged <code>69a3393</code>; PR #55 (P2-044 idle dependence / HAC / ESS, design-consult-first, review + fix round) merged <code>56d103e</code>. At the Ed-directed pause (stop card checkpoint #4 + amendments) PRs #50–#53 and #56–#58 stood open and lead-gated with the resume order pinned; after resume, the integration tree (<code>c028-integration</code> @ <code>190a0fc</code>, main post-#55 + 7 branches) caught 38 cross-stream failures, the fix round + cross-stream review cleared them, and the full wave merged SHA-guarded (#50, #51, #52, #53, #56, #57, #58 — P2-037 last), with final main verified green and content-identical to the reviewed tree; follow-up PR #59 (from the cross-stream review) is under review and DOC-008 rounds remain in flight. Delegation infrastructure landed on main: adapter, codex-run-v3, usage guard, scope backstop.</p> <p>Closeout amendment (2026-07-11): C-028 is <strong>CLOSED</strong>. PRs #41-#58 are merged; current main&#39;s canonical suite is 1,220 OK (<code>skipped=10</code>) and the corpus gate is 6/6. PR #59 remains open with a 1,224-test green worktree replay (<code>skipped=12</code>), and <code>impl/doc008-kernel</code> is pushed awaiting PR. These open follow-ups do not reopen the card. Every Window-A software gate and P0-003 are satisfied; quiet-machine execution with Ed remains deliberately separate from landed-software status. NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). Only layer to catch it.</li> <li><strong>Refuter tier:</strong> narrowed 2 blockers via CONTRADICTORY paired verdicts — P2-041 B1 (contract refuter confirmed, reachability refuter refuted the broad form → landed as the narrowed shared fail-closed cooldown verifier, <code>f2c4701</code>) and P2-037 F1 (design vs repro refuters split the same way → F1 narrowed before the fix round). The disagreement itself was the signal; neither single refuter would have produced the narrowed form.</li> <li><strong>Delta re-audits:</strong> 2 fresh blockers in paths newly reachable only after the fix round (P2-037 delta re-audit: blocker=2/should-fix=3), plus the recurring symlink pattern — cooldown provenance <code>Path.resolve</code> unwrapped against symlink loop/OSError, wrapped fail-closed with a cross-version regression test (<code>5f1f161</code>). Neither finding existed in the pre-fix tree; the re-audit layer is what sees post-fix reachability.</li> <li><strong>Lead gates:</strong> P2-044 F1 cadence arithmetic verified directly (all-intervals population; binding Qwen-r3 values asserted exactly: median 0.1199250625, ratio 1.0581313969 — <code>dc1ab95</code>); live NV-5 localhost gate 3/3 OK closing the open lead gate on #49 (<code>10e0ad2</code>); live doctor run. All three are lead-live-only — no static layer could produce them.</li> <li><strong>Integration tree:</strong> 38 pre-merge cross-stream test failures caught at the combined head, dominated by REPRO-002&#39;s fail-closed environment/inventory checks meeting post-cut fields from sibling streams. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<h1>JouleWise: Project Status, Plan, And Architecture</h1> <p>Audience: project advisor. This is the standalone monitoring document - it summarizes what the project is, how it is built, where it stands, and what it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository are provided for anyone who wants the full evidence trail.</p> <ul> <li>Freshness owner: phase completion lives in the phase exit checklists; live gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>; the canonical suite command and CI own the current verification result. This page deliberately does not duplicate volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.</li> <li>Repository state: <code>main</code> contains the repaired measurement instrument (D-078 phase 0) and the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10; council C-033). The repaired-instrument collection has 229 members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are useful diagnostic evidence that the instrument works, but they are not claim-bearing and do not yet publish a floor. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine collection following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>; if it passes, it will produce the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</li> <li>Project phase: see the phase exit checklists for exact completion state; live eligibility and next work come from the generated state kernel, not this reader-facing summary.</li> <li>Repository: <code>github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</code> (branch <code>main</code>)</li> <li>Live status site: <a href="https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app">https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app</a> (Lakebed capsule; it is an Ed-deployed snapshot, not the repository authority. <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code> records known differences; agents refresh that report when front-facing state changes and never regenerate or deploy the site.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="current-repository-view-30-second-read">Current Repository View — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The repaired instrument has completed its first collection era, but the first claim-grade floor is still ahead.</strong> The D-078 phase-0 repair fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22. Four bracketed windows then collected 229 strict members (a5-a8). They are retained as non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence: they showed that the repaired path works and exposed the remaining drift-screen problem, but they are not a published floor set.</p> <p>That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims. The next quiet session will mint its bound inside the window and collect three start references, one midpoint reference, and three end references. The older 222-bundle floor table below remains visible as a caveated historical record, not the current measurement posture.</p> <p>AXI-SB remains <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.</p> <h3>Published Window-A floor summary</h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>CAVEAT (2026-07-19 soundness audit):</strong> a trace-time-anchor defect was found in the powermetrics evidence path (power timestamps misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale).
